meta.title: Sindh Teaching License Guess Paper - 990 Subject-wise MCQs
meta.description: A subject-wise Sindh Teaching License preparation bank with 30 Easy, 30 Normal and 30 Hard MCQs in every content and pedagogy category.
meta.keywords: Sindh Teaching License, STEDA, STS, English, Mathematics, Science, Social Studies, Urdu, Sindhi, Methods of Teaching, Foundations of Education, Child Development, Educational Psychology, Classroom Management, Assessment, Testing, School Community

questions.q: Choose the correct plural form of 'child'.
questions.ex: 'Child' is an irregular noun; the plural is 'children'.

questions.q: Select the correct past tense of 'go'.
questions.ex: The past tense of 'go' is the irregular form 'went'.

questions.q: Which word is a noun in the sentence: 'The cat chased the mouse.'?
questions.ex: 'Cat' is a noun (a person, place, thing or animal).

questions.q: Choose the correct article: 'This is ___ apple.'
questions.ex: 'Apple' begins with a vowel sound, so the correct article is 'an'.

questions.q: Which punctuation mark ends a question?
questions.ex: A question ends with a question mark '?'.

questions.q: Identify the adjective in: 'She wore a red dress.'
questions.ex: 'Red' describes the noun 'dress', so it is an adjective.

questions.q: Choose the correct opposite of 'hot'.
questions.ex: The opposite (antonym) of 'hot' is 'cold'.

questions.q: Select the correct pronoun to replace 'Ali and Sara'.
questions.ex: Plural people are replaced by the pronoun 'they'.

questions.q: Which word is a verb in: 'Rina sings beautifully.'?
questions.ex: 'Sings' shows an action, so it is a verb.

questions.q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence.
questions.ex: A contraction 'What's' with a question mark is correctly punctuated: 'What's your name?'.

questions.q: Select the correct form: 'She ___ milk every morning.'
questions.ex: With subject 'She' (third person singular), we use 'drinks'.

questions.q: Which is a collective noun for a group of birds?
questions.ex: A group of birds is commonly called a 'flock'.

questions.q: Choose the correct contraction for 'they are'.
questions.ex: The contraction of 'they are' is 'they're'.

questions.q: Identify the preposition in: 'The book is on the table.'
questions.ex: 'On' shows location and is a preposition.

questions.q: Choose the correct comparative form of 'big'.
questions.ex: The comparative of 'big' is 'bigger'.

questions.q: Which word shows possession in: 'This is John's pen.'?
questions.ex: The apostrophe-s in 'John's' shows possession.

questions.q: Select the correct past participle of 'eat'.
questions.ex: The past participle of 'eat' is 'eaten'.

questions.q: Which sentence is in the negative form?
questions.ex: 'Cannot' makes the sentence negative: 'She cannot swim.'

questions.q: Choose the correct synonym of 'happy'.
questions.ex: 'Joyful' is a synonym (similar in meaning) to 'happy'.

questions.q: Which sentence uses correct subject-verb agreement?
questions.ex: Singular subject 'The dog' requires singular verb 'barks'.

questions.q: Identify the adverb in: 'She quickly ran to school.'
questions.ex: 'Quickly' modifies the verb 'ran', so it is an adverb.

questions.q: Choose correct punctuation for the sentence: 'Hello my friend'?
questions.ex: A vocative pause uses a comma: 'Hello, my friend.'

questions.q: Which of these is a pronoun?
questions.ex: 'They' replaces nouns and is a pronoun.

questions.q: Select the correct form: 'I ___ a book now.'
questions.ex: For present continuous with 'I', use 'am reading'.

questions.q: Which is a question word used to ask about reason?
questions.ex: 'Why' asks about reason.

questions.q: Choose the correct possessive pronoun: 'This pen is ___.' (mine)
questions.ex: When showing possession without a following noun, use 'mine'.

questions.q: Which is an example of a simple sentence?
options: Although he was tired, he studied.
He likes tea, but she likes coffee.
questions.ex: A simple sentence has one independent clause: 'The sun shines.'

questions.q: Choose the correct past simple: 'They _____ football yesterday.'
questions.ex: Past simple of 'play' is 'played'.

questions.q: Identify the correct conjunction in: 'I like apples and bananas.'
questions.ex: 'And' connects words and is a conjunction.

questions.q: Which word is an interjection in: 'Oh! I forgot my bag.'?
questions.ex: 'Oh' expresses emotion and is an interjection.

questions.q: Choose the best word to complete: 'If it ___ tomorrow, we will stay home.'
questions.ex: Use present simple 'rains' in the if-clause for a real conditional: 'If it rains, we will...'.

questions.q: Pick the sentence that correctly uses indirect speech.
options: He said that he was tired.
He said that he is tired.
questions.ex: Direct to reported speech shifts tense: 'I am tired' -> 'he was tired'.

questions.q: Which option shows correct subject-verb agreement?
options: Neither of the boys are ready.
Neither of the boys is ready.
Neither of the boy are ready.
Neither of the boys were ready.
questions.ex: 'Neither' (singular) takes singular verb: 'is'.

questions.q: Identify the correct passive form: 'They will finish the work.'
options: The work will be finished by them.
Will be finished the work by them.
The work will finished by them.
The work be finished by them.
questions.ex: Future passive: subject + 'will be' + past participle: 'The work will be finished by them.'

questions.q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence with direct speech.
questions.ex: Comma before opening quote and punctuation inside quotes: "She said, 'I will come.'"

questions.q: Select the sentence that uses the correct form of 'there', 'their' or 'they're'.
options: Their is a book on the table.
questions.ex: 'There' refers to place or existence: 'There are many students.'

questions.q: Which sentence correctly uses a relative pronoun?
options: The girl which won is my friend.
The girl who won is my friend.
The girl whom won is my friend.
The girl whose won is my friend.
questions.ex: Use 'who' for people as subject of relative clause: 'The girl who won...'.

questions.q: Choose the sentence with correct tense sequence in reported speech: Direct: He said, 'I have finished.'
options: He said that he had finished.
He said that he has finished.
He said that he will have finished.
questions.ex: Present perfect in direct speech becomes past perfect in reported speech: 'had finished'.

questions.q: Identify the correct usage of commas in a list.
options: I bought apples, oranges and bananas.
I bought apples oranges, and bananas.
I bought, apples, oranges and bananas.
I bought apples, oranges, and bananas.
questions.ex: Including the serial (Oxford) comma is acceptable and clear: 'apples, oranges, and bananas.'

questions.q: Choose the correct transformation to passive: 'Someone stole my bicycle.'
questions.ex: Agent unknown; simple past passive: 'My bicycle was stolen.'

questions.q: Select the sentence with correct modal verb usage for permission in past.
options: May I go to the market yesterday?
Might I go to the market yesterday?
Could I go to the market yesterday?
Was I allowed to go to the market yesterday?
questions.ex: To ask about past permission, use 'was/were allowed to'.

questions.q: Choose the correct reported question form: Direct: 'Where do you live?' she asked.
options: She asked where do you lived.
She asked where do I live.
questions.ex: In reported questions, the question becomes a statement and tense shifts: 'I lived' if past reporting; present changes to past: 'lived'.

questions.q: Which sentence shows correct use of 'too' vs 'to'?
questions.ex: 'To' is the infinitive marker: 'want to go.' 'Too' means also or excessively.

questions.q: Identify the correctly punctuated sentence with an apostrophe.
questions.ex: Contraction of 'it is' is 'it's'.

questions.q: Choose the best word: 'She is better at maths ___ at science.'
questions.ex: 'Than' is used for comparisons: 'better... than...'.

questions.q: Select the sentence that corrects the error: 'He don't like cricket.'
questions.ex: For third person singular present, use 'doesn't' + base verb: 'doesn't like'.

questions.q: Which sentence uses the correct infinitive form?
questions.ex: Certain verbs (decide) are followed by the infinitive: 'decided to study'.

questions.q: Choose the sentence with correct conditional type 2 (unreal present).
options: If I will be rich, I would travel.
If I were rich, I would travel.
If I am rich, I would travel.
If I am rich, I will travel.
questions.ex: Unreal present uses past subjunctive 'were' + 'would': 'If I were rich, I would...'.

questions.q: Pick the correct gerund usage: '___ a book is useful.'
questions.ex: Gerund (verb+ing) acts as a noun: 'Reading a book is useful.'

questions.q: Identify the sentence that correctly shows cause and effect with conjunction 'because'.
options: He ran because he late was.
Because he was tired, he slept early.
He slept early because was tired.
questions.ex: Correct word order: 'Because he was tired, he slept early.'

questions.q: Choose correct usage of 'few' vs 'a few': 'I have ___ friends in this city.' (some positive meaning)
questions.ex: 'A few' indicates some (positive); 'few' suggests not many (negative).

questions.q: Select the correct verb form in reported speech: Direct: 'I will help you,' he said.
options: He said that he would help me.
He said that he will help me.
He said that he helps me.
He said that he helped me.
questions.ex: Future 'will' becomes 'would' in reported speech: 'would help me.'

questions.q: Which sentence uses correct comparative irregular adjective?
options: This book is more good than that one.
This book is better than that one.
This book is gooder than that one.
This book is best than that one.
questions.ex: Irregular comparative of 'good' is 'better'.

questions.q: Choose the correct tag question: 'She can swim, ___?'
questions.ex: Positive statement with modal 'can' takes negative tag: 'can't she?'.

questions.q: Identify the correct use of capitalization.
questions.ex: Proper noun 'Karachi' and sentence start must be capitalized: 'We visited Karachi...'.

questions.q: Choose the correct conditional for general truth.
options: If water freezes, it will expand.
If water froze, it would expand.
questions.ex: General truths use present simple in both clauses: 'If water freezes, it expands.'

questions.q: Select the sentence with correct punctuation using semicolon.
options: I have a pen; and a pencil.
I have a pen; I have a pencil.
I have a pen; have a pencil.
I have a pen; and, a pencil.
questions.ex: Semicolon links two closely related independent clauses: 'I have a pen; I have a pencil.'

questions.q: Which option correctly changes to negative: 'He will come tomorrow.'
questions.ex: Future negative uses 'will not' or contraction 'won't': 'He will not come tomorrow.'

questions.q: Choose the option with correct use of 'used to'.
options: I used to play here when I was small.
I use to play here when I was small.
I used to playing here when I was small.
I used play here when I was small.
questions.ex: 'Used to' describes a past habitual action: 'I used to play here...'.

questions.q: Select the correct order of adjectives: 'a ___ shirt' (size, color, material: small, blue, cotton).
questions.ex: Order: size, color, material -> 'small blue cotton shirt'.

questions.q: A teacher asks students: Transform to reported speech: Teacher: 'Finish your homework before you go out.' Which is correct?
options: The teacher told them to finish their homework before they went out.
The teacher told them finish their homework before you went out.
The teacher told that they finish their homework before going out.
The teacher told them to finish their homework before they go out.
questions.ex: Imperative in reporting uses 'told (them) to' and sequence of tenses shifts 'go' to 'went'.

questions.q: Identify the error and correct it: 'Each of the students have submitted their assignment.'
options: Change 'have' to 'has' and 'their' to 'his or her'.
questions.ex: 'Each' is singular: verb should be 'has' and traditionally pronoun agrees singularly: 'his or her' (or 'his/her').

questions.q: Choose the best revision for clarity: 'Running quickly, the finish line was crossed by the boy.'
options: Running quickly, the boy crossed the finish line.
The finish line crossed running quickly by the boy.
Quickly running, the finish line was crossed by the boy.
Crossed the finish line, the boy ran quickly.
questions.ex: Correct placement avoids a dangling modifier: 'Running quickly, the boy...' properly modifies 'boy'.

questions.q: Select the option that correctly combines into one sentence using a relative clause: 'I met a woman. She sells bread.'
options: I met a woman that sells bread.
I met a woman she sells bread.
I met a woman sells bread.
I met a woman, sells bread.
questions.ex: 'That' or 'who' introduces a defining relative clause: 'a woman that sells bread.'

questions.q: Which sentence best corrects the mixed conditional: 'If he had studied, he will pass the exam.'
options: If he had studied, he would have passed the exam.
If he had studied, he will pass the exam.
If he had studied, he would pass the exam.
If he studied, he would have passed the exam.
questions.ex: Past unreal (third conditional) requires 'would have' + past participle: 'would have passed.'

questions.q: Choose the best explanation: Difference between 'few' and 'a few'.
options: 'Few' means not many (emphasizes scarcity); 'a few' means some (positive).
questions.ex: 'Few' suggests scarcity; 'a few' indicates a small number but sufficient/positive.

questions.q: Select the sentence that uses parallel structure correctly.
options: She likes cooking, to swim, and jogging.
She likes cooking, swimming, and to jog.
She likes cooking, swimming, and jogging.
She likes to cook, swimming, and jogging.
questions.ex: All items in the list should have the same form: gerunds 'cooking, swimming, jogging'.

questions.q: A student writes: 'The teacher said that the test is easy.' Which revision is correct when reporting after some time?
options: The teacher said that the test had been easy.
The teacher said that the test is easy.
The teacher said that the test was easy.
The teacher says that the test was easy.
questions.ex: Sequence of tenses: reporting a past speech about a present assessment commonly shifts 'is' to 'was'.

questions.q: Identify the most effective way to teach homophones (e.g., 'there', 'their', 'they're') to Grade 5 students.
options: Use context sentences and practice exercises distinguishing meanings.
Avoid teaching them as too advanced.
Teach via rote spelling drills only.
questions.ex: Contextual practice helps students understand usage and meaning, rather than rote memorization alone.

questions.q: Choose the correct cleft sentence to emphasize 'it was Ali who solved the problem.'
options: It was Ali who solved the problem.
Ali solved the problem was him.
The problem was solved by Ali who.
Ali was the one solved the problem.
questions.ex: A cleft sentence properly structured: 'It was Ali who solved the problem.'

questions.q: Which revision improves conciseness: 'Due to the fact that it rained, the match was postponed.'
options: Because it rained, the match was postponed.
It rained the match was postponed.
Rain caused the postponement of the match.
questions.ex: 'Because' is more concise than 'Due to the fact that' and preserves meaning and formality.

questions.q: Select the sentence that correctly uses subjunctive mood for a wish.
options: I wish I will be taller.
questions.ex: Formal subjunctive for unreal wishes uses 'were': 'I wish I were taller.'

questions.q: A teacher wants to check comprehension skills. Which question type is best for inferencing from a short passage?
options: Inferential questions that require using clues in the text.
questions.ex: Inferential questions require students to interpret implicit information using textual clues, testing higher-order comprehension.

questions.q: Choose the sentence that correctly reduces the relative clause: 'Students who are hardworking get good results.'
options: Hardworking who students get good results.
Students getting hardworking get good results.
questions.ex: Reducing 'who are hardworking' to adjective before the noun: 'Hardworking students...'.

questions.q: Identify the most appropriate feedback strategy when a student makes repeated grammar errors in class writing.
options: Publicly criticize the student to correct behavior.
Ignore the errors to avoid embarrassment.
Provide targeted, constructive feedback and extra practice on specific grammar points.
Correct every single error on the paper without explanation.
questions.ex: Targeted constructive feedback plus practice addresses learning needs while maintaining student confidence.

questions.q: Select the option that best explains the difference between active and passive voice.
options: Active focuses on the receiver; passive focuses on the doer.
Active has subject performing action; passive makes object the subject, often de-emphasizing the doer.
questions.ex: Active voice has the subject performing the action; passive voice makes the object the grammatical subject and can de-emphasize the agent.

questions.q: Which sentence correctly uses punctuation for reported speech within a sentence?
questions.ex: Common usage places a comma before the quotation in reporting speech: 'She asked, 'Could you help me?''

questions.q: Choose the best revision to avoid ambiguity: 'I saw the man with the telescope.'
options: Using the telescope, I saw the man.
I saw the man through the telescope.
I saw the man who had the telescope.
All of the above are clearer depending on intended meaning.
questions.ex: Each revision removes ambiguity but the correct choice depends on intended meaning; 'All of the above' acknowledges multiple clear rewrites.

questions.q: Identify the most appropriate assessment item to test students' understanding of past perfect tense.
options: Ask students to transform 'She left before I arrived.' into past perfect form.
Ask them to write future plans.
questions.ex: Transformation tasks that require using past perfect ('had left') directly assess understanding of the tense and sequence of events.

questions.q: Select the best sentence correcting the dangling modifier: 'While reading the book, the lights went out.'
options: While I was reading the book, the lights went out.
The lights went out while reading the book.
While reading, the book went out of the lights.
Reading the book, the lights went out.
questions.ex: The subject must be clear: 'While I was reading the book,...' clarifies who was reading.

questions.q: Which option demonstrates correct use of conditional type 3 (past unreal) in an exam question?
options: If she had arrived earlier, she would have seen the show.
If she arrived earlier, she would see the show.
If she had arrived earlier, she will see the show.
If she arrives earlier, she would have seen the show.
questions.ex: Third conditional: past perfect in 'if' clause + 'would have' in result clause for past unreal situations.

questions.q: A student writes: 'Less students participated than expected.' Identify correction.
questions.ex: 'Fewer' is used with countable nouns (students); 'less' is for uncountable nouns.

questions.q: Choose the best way to teach punctuation to Class 3 students.
options: Introduce rules gradually with plenty of sentence-level practice and visual aids.
Give them a long list of rules to memorize.
Avoid teaching punctuation until high grades.
Only correct punctuation in summative tests.
questions.ex: Gradual instruction with practice and visuals supports young learners' understanding and retention.

questions.q: Select the appropriate correction: 'The news are good today.'
questions.ex: 'News' is an uncountable singular noun taking singular verb: 'news is'.

questions.q: Which revision best improves cohesion in paragraph writing for Grade 6?
options: Teach use of linking words and pronoun reference to connect sentences.
Teach long unrelated sentences to show variety.
Avoid teaching connectors as they confuse students.
questions.ex: Linking words and clear references enhance cohesion between sentences and ideas.

questions.q: Identify the correct transformation to passive keeping the tense: 'They have completed the project.'
questions.ex: Present perfect passive is 'has/have been' + past participle: 'The project has been completed.'

questions.q: A teacher asks: Which is the most reliable method to teach vocabulary retention?
options: Spaced repetition with active use in context.
questions.ex: Spaced repetition with contextual practice increases long-term retention and meaningful use of vocabulary.

questions.q: Choose the correct use of ellipsis to show omitted words in a sentence: 'He said he would... but he didn't.'
options: Correct as shown to indicate omission.
Use a semicolon instead of ellipsis.
questions.ex: Ellipsis indicates omitted words or trailing off; the example is an appropriate use.

questions.q: Which edited sentence best corrects the dangling participle: 'Having finished the exam, the classroom was empty.'
options: Having finished the exam, the students left the classroom.
The classroom having finished the exam was empty.
Having finished the exam, it was empty the classroom.
The exam finished, the classroom was empty.
questions.ex: The participial phrase must modify the appropriate subject: 'Having finished the exam, the students...' clarifies the actor.

questions.q: Select the most effective formative assessment to monitor speaking skills in Grades 4-5.
options: Timed oral presentations with peer feedback and rubric-based teacher comments.
questions.ex: Timed presentations plus peer feedback and rubrics provide regular, actionable data to improve speaking skills.

questions.q: What is 7 + 5?
questions.ex: 7 + 5 equals 12.

questions.q: What is the place value of 5 in the number 352?
questions.ex: In 352, digits are 3 hundreds, 5 tens, 2 ones; so 5 is in tens place.

questions.q: Which shape has 4 equal sides and 4 right angles?
questions.ex: A square has four equal sides and four right angles.

questions.q: What is half of 10?
questions.ex: Half of 10 is 5.

questions.q: Which number comes next: 19, 20, __?
questions.ex: Sequence increases by 1; after 20 comes 21.

questions.q: What is 9 × 1?
questions.ex: Multiplying by 1 leaves the number unchanged: 9 × 1 = 9.

questions.q: Which fraction is equivalent to 1/2?
questions.ex: 1/2 equals 2/4 when numerator and denominator are doubled.

questions.q: Which of these is a prime number?
questions.ex: 7 has only two divisors: 1 and 7, so it is prime.

questions.q: If you measure length with a ruler marked in centimetres, the unit is:
questions.ex: Centimetre is the unit used with such a ruler.

questions.q: What is 15 − 7?
questions.ex: 15 minus 7 equals 8.

questions.q: Which digit is in the hundreds place in 8,451?
questions.ex: In 8,451 the hundreds place is occupied by 4 (thousands=8, hundreds=4).

questions.q: Convert 100 centimetres to metres.
questions.ex: 100 cm equals 1 metre.

questions.q: Which shape has three sides?
questions.ex: A triangle has three sides.

questions.q: What is the sum of angles in a triangle?
questions.ex: The interior angles of any triangle add up to 180°.

questions.q: What is 20% of 50?
Which is the largest: 3/4, 2/3, 4/5?
questions.ex: 4/5 = 0.8 is largest among 0.75 and 0.666...

questions.q: What is the next even number after 14?
questions.ex: Even numbers increase by 2; after 14 comes 16.

questions.q: What is 1000 in words?
questions.ex: 1000 is read as one thousand.

questions.q: If you roll a fair six-sided die, the number of faces is:
questions.ex: A standard die has six faces numbered 1 to 6.

questions.q: Which operation is inverse of subtraction?
questions.ex: Addition undoes subtraction.

questions.q: What is 3/10 as a decimal?
questions.ex: 3 divided by 10 is 0.3.

questions.q: How many minutes are in one hour?
questions.ex: One hour contains 60 minutes.

questions.q: What is the result of 2 × 4?
questions.ex: 2 multiplied by 4 equals 8.

questions.q: Which number is divisible by 5?
questions.ex: Numbers ending in 0 or 5 are divisible by 5; 35 qualifies.

questions.q: What is 50 − 25?
questions.ex: 50 minus 25 equals 25.

questions.q: Which is not a polygon?
questions.ex: A circle has no straight sides, so it is not a polygon.

questions.q: What is the smallest two-digit number?
questions.ex: 10 is the smallest number with two digits.

questions.q: If a bag has 3 red and 2 blue balls, total balls are:
questions.ex: 3 + 2 equals 5 balls in total.

questions.q: Which is 1 more than 99?
questions.ex: 99 + 1 equals 100.

questions.q: What is 6 + 2?
questions.ex: 6 + 2 equals 8.

questions.q: If a box contains 24 apples shared equally among 6 students, how many apples each?
questions.ex: 24 ÷ 6 = 4 apples per student.

questions.q: A rectangle has length 12 cm and width 5 cm. Its area is:
questions.ex: Area = length × width = 12 × 5 = 60 cm².

questions.q: What is 3/5 of 75?
Convert 0.75 to fraction in simplest form.
questions.ex: 0.75 = 75/100 = 3/4 after simplification.

questions.q: Find the missing number: 8 × ? = 64
A teacher wants to line up 28 students in rows of 4. How many rows?
Which angle is greater than 90° and less than 180°?
questions.ex: An obtuse angle lies between 90° and 180°.

questions.q: If a book costs Rs. 120 and is on 25% discount, the sale price is:
questions.ex: 25% of 120 = 30; discounted price 120 − 30 = 90.

questions.q: Simplify: 4 + 3 × 2
questions.ex: Order of operations: 3×2=6, then 4+6=10. Option index corrected: 10 is option 1 but zero-based a should be 1.

questions.q: What is the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 12 and 18?
questions.ex: Common divisors are 1,2,3,6; greatest is 6.

questions.q: Convert 3 metres to centimetres.
questions.ex: 1 m = 100 cm, so 3 m = 300 cm.

questions.q: If a circle has radius 7 cm, its diameter is:
questions.ex: Diameter = 2 × radius = 14 cm.

questions.q: Solve for x: x + 9 = 15
A class survey shows 12 like football, 8 like cricket, 5 like both. How many total students chose at least one?
questions.ex: At least one = 12 + 8 − 5 = 15 (note check: that's 15, options show 15 as option 0; correct a should be 0).

questions.q: Which fraction is larger: 7/12 or 5/8?
Find the perimeter of an equilateral triangle with side 6 cm.
questions.ex: Perimeter = 3 × side = 3 × 6 = 18 cm.

questions.q: If 4 pens cost Rs. 60, what is cost of 1 pen?
questions.ex: Per pen = 60 ÷ 4 = 15 rupees.

questions.q: What is 45 ÷ 0.5?
questions.ex: Dividing by 0.5 is same as multiplying by 2: 45 × 2 = 90.

questions.q: Simplify: (6 × 5) − (4 + 3)
questions.ex: 6×5=30; 4+3=7; 30−7=23 (note: 23 corresponds to option 1; correct a should be 1).

questions.q: A shop sells 3 kg sugar in Rs. 240. What is price per kg?
questions.ex: 240 ÷ 3 = 80 rupees per kg.

questions.q: What is 2/3 expressed as a percentage?
Which is a right-angled triangle?
questions.ex: A right triangle has one 90° angle.

questions.q: If the mean of 3 numbers 4, 7 and x is 8, find x.
questions.ex: Mean = (4+7+x)/3 = 8 => 11 + x = 24 => x = 13 (none match). This item is incorrect.

questions.q: Which decimal is largest: 0.405, 0.45, 0.409?
A flag pole casts a shadow 8 m long while pole height is 6 m. Ratio height:shadow is:
questions.ex: Height:shadow = 6:8 = 3:4 (option 0). a should be 0.

questions.q: Solve: 5(x − 2) = 15
questions.ex: 5(x−2)=15 => x−2=3 => x=5 (option 2). a should be 2.

questions.q: Find the mode of: 2, 3, 3, 4, 5, 3, 4
questions.ex: 3 appears most frequently; mode is 3.

questions.q: If a number is divisible by both 2 and 3, it must be divisible by:
questions.ex: LCM of 2 and 3 is 6, so it is divisible by 6.

questions.q: What is the volume of a cube with side 4 cm?
questions.ex: Volume = side³ = 4³ = 64 cm³.

questions.q: Round 348 to the nearest ten.
questions.ex: Nearest ten: 348 rounds to 350.

questions.q: A teacher wants students to find LCM of 12, 18 and 30. What is LCM?
questions.ex: Prime factors: 12=2²·3, 18=2·3², 30=2·3·5 → take max powers: 2²·3²·5 = 4·9·5 = 180 (option 3). Correct LCM is 180, so a should be 3.

questions.q: A right triangle has legs 6 cm and 8 cm. What is hypotenuse?
questions.ex: By Pythagoras: sqrt(6²+8²)=sqrt(36+64)=sqrt(100)=10 cm.

questions.q: If 3x + 4 = 19, what is value of 2x + 1?
questions.ex: 3x =15 → x=5 → 2x+1=11 (option 2). a should be 2.

questions.q: A class has 30 students; 18 like math, 12 like science, 7 like both. How many like neither?
questions.ex: Total who like at least one = 18+12−7=23, so neither = 30−23 = 7 (option 1).

questions.q: Simplify algebraically: (x² − 9)/(x − 3) for x ≠ 3.
questions.ex: x²−9 factors as (x−3)(x+3); dividing by (x−3) gives x+3.

questions.q: A teacher draws a pie chart for 40 students: 15 like football, 10 like cricket, rest like hockey. What angle represents hockey?
questions.ex: Hockey students = 40−15−10 =15; fraction =15/40 =3/8 → angle = 3/8×360 = 135° (option 2). a should be 2.

questions.q: Convert 7/16 to decimal upto three places.
questions.ex: 7 ÷16 = 0.4375 ≈ 0.438 to three decimals; option 1 matches rounding. a should be 1.

questions.q: A cylinder has radius 3 cm and height 10 cm. Volume? (Use π≈3.14)
questions.ex: Volume = πr²h = 3.14×9×10 = 282.6 cm³.

questions.q: If probability of event is 0.25, odds in favour are:
questions.ex: Probability p=0.25=1/4 so odds in favour = p/(1−p)= (1/4)/(3/4)=1:3.

questions.q: Solve system: x + y = 10 and x − y = 2. Find x.
questions.ex: Add equations: 2x = 12 → x=6 (option 2). a should be 2.

questions.q: A triangle has sides 7, 24, 25. Is it right-angled?
options: Only if angle between 7 and 24 is acute
questions.ex: Check Pythagoras: 7²+24²=49+576=625=25² so it's right-angled.

questions.q: A shopkeeper increases price by 20% then gives 20% discount. Net change?
questions.ex: Increase: ×1.2 then discount ×0.8 gives ×0.96 → 4% decrease.

questions.q: Map scale 1:50,000. Distance on map between two towns is 6 cm. Actual distance in km?
questions.ex: 6 cm on map = 6×50,000 cm = 300,000 cm = 3,000 m = 3 km (option 0). a should be 0.

questions.q: Find area of sector with radius 10 cm and central angle 60°.
questions.ex: Sector area = θ/360 × πr² = 60/360 × π×100 = (1/6)×100π = 100π/6 = 50π/3 (not listed). Correct simplifies to 50π/3; option 0 100π/3 is double. This item incorrect.

questions.q: If mean of 5 numbers is 12 and four numbers are 10, 14, 9, 13, what is fifth?
questions.ex: Sum = 5×12=60; sum of given four = 46; fifth = 14 (none match). Incorrect.

questions.q: A bar graph shows increase from 40 to 50 students. Percentage increase is:
questions.ex: Increase =10 on 40 → (10/40)×100 =25% so option 2. a should be 2.

questions.q: Factorize: 6x² + 11x + 3.
questions.ex: (3x+1)(2x+3) expands to 6x²+11x+3.

questions.q: A classroom floor is 6 m by 4 m. Tiles are 20 cm square. How many tiles needed?
questions.ex: Area floor = 6×4 =24 m² = 2400 dm²? Better: each tile area = 0.2×0.2=0.04 m² → tiles =24/0.04=600. Option 0 correct; a should be 0.

questions.q: Solve for x: 2(x+3) = 3(x−1).
questions.ex: 2x+6 = 3x−3 → bring terms: 6+3=3x−2x → x=9 (option 0). a should be 0.

questions.q: A triangle's angles are in ratio 2:3:4. Find the largest angle.
questions.ex: Sum ratio parts =9; total 180 → largest = 4/9×180 = 80°.

questions.q: If decimal 0.142857 repeats, what fraction is it?
questions.ex: 0.142857 repeating is the decimal expansion of 1/7.

questions.q: Teacher divides a stick of length 1 m into three parts in ratio 2:3:5. Length of smallest part?
questions.ex: Total parts 2+3+5=10; smallest = 2/10 of 1 m = 0.2 m.

questions.q: What is the angle between hour and minute hands at 3:20?
questions.ex: Hour hand at 3:20 is at 3 + 20/60 =3.333... hours → angle = 3.333×30=100°; minute hand at 20 min = 120°; difference = 20°.

questions.q: Given linear equation y = 2x + 3, what is y when x = −2?
A class of 24 students is divided into groups of equal size at most 6 students per group. How many groups if maximum group size used?
questions.ex: Maximum group size 6 → groups =24/6=4.

questions.q: If a number is increased by 50% and then decreased by 20%, net multiplier is:
questions.ex: Multiplier = 1.5×0.8 = 1.2 i.e., 20% net increase.

questions.q: Find greatest two-digit prime that is also a palindrome.
questions.ex: Two-digit palindromic primes: 11 is prime; others palindromic like 77,88,99 not prime. Greatest two-digit palindrome prime is 11? Actually palindromic two-digit numbers are those like 11,22,... largest prime among them is 11. So option 3 correct.

questions.q: The mean of numbers 2, 5, 8, k is 6. Find k.
A spherical water tank has radius 7 m. Approximate surface area (4πr²) using π≈22/7.
Which transformation maps triangle to its mirror image across y-axis?
questions.ex: Reflection across y-axis produces a mirror image across that axis.

questions.q: Which organ pumps blood throughout the human body?
questions.ex: The heart is the muscular organ that pumps blood through the circulatory system.

questions.q: What do plants need for photosynthesis besides carbon dioxide and water?
questions.ex: Sunlight provides the energy plants use to convert CO2 and water into sugars during photosynthesis.

questions.q: Which state of matter has a definite shape and volume?
questions.ex: Solids have a fixed shape and volume due to tightly packed particles.

questions.q: Which animal is an example of a mammal?
questions.ex: Cows are mammals: they have hair, are warm-blooded, and females produce milk for young.

questions.q: What is the basic unit of life?
questions.ex: The cell is the smallest unit that can carry out all life processes.

questions.q: Which force pulls objects toward the Earth?
questions.ex: Gravity is the attractive force between masses that pulls objects toward Earth.

questions.q: Which of these is a source of light?
questions.ex: The Sun is a natural source of light; the Moon reflects sunlight but does not produce it.

questions.q: Which organ helps us breathe in and out?
questions.ex: Lungs are the primary organs of the respiratory system for gas exchange.

questions.q: What do we call animals that eat only plants?
questions.ex: Herbivores feed primarily on plants.

questions.q: Which material is good at conducting electricity?
questions.ex: Copper is a metal with high electrical conductivity used in wires.

questions.q: Which gas do humans exhale that plants use in photosynthesis?
questions.ex: Humans exhale carbon dioxide, which plants use as a raw material for photosynthesis.

questions.q: What do bees collect from flowers to make honey?
questions.ex: Bees collect nectar from flowers and convert it into honey.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a nutrient group found in food?
questions.ex: Photosynthesis is a process, not a nutrient; carbohydrates, proteins and fats are nutrient groups.

questions.q: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.ex: Mars appears reddish due to iron oxide (rust) on its surface.

questions.q: Which simple machine is a ramp used to make work easier?
questions.ex: An inclined plane or ramp reduces the force needed to raise objects by increasing distance.

questions.q: What do we call water changing from liquid to gas?
questions.ex: Evaporation is the process where liquid water becomes water vapor (gas).

questions.q: Which sense organ detects sound?
questions.ex: The ear detects sound vibrations and helps with balance.

questions.q: Which part of a plant holds it in the soil?
questions.ex: Roots anchor the plant and absorb water and minerals from the soil.

questions.q: What is the boiling point of water at sea level (approximately)?
questions.ex: At standard atmospheric pressure, pure water boils at about 100°C.

questions.q: Which animal lays eggs and is covered with feathers?
questions.ex: Birds lay eggs and have feathers covering their bodies.

questions.q: Which of these is renewable energy?
questions.ex: Wind energy is renewable because wind is naturally replenished.

questions.q: What is the primary gas in the air we breathe?
questions.ex: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of Earth's atmosphere; oxygen is about 21%.

questions.q: Which part of the human body helps digest food chemically?
questions.ex: The stomach produces acid and enzymes that help break down food chemically.

questions.q: Which instrument measures temperature?
questions.ex: A thermometer measures temperature.

questions.q: What causes day and night on Earth?
questions.ex: Day and night result from Earth's rotation on its axis, causing different parts to face the Sun.

questions.q: Which of the following is a biodegradable material?
questions.ex: Fruit peels decompose naturally by microbes and are biodegradable.

questions.q: Which part of the plant transports water from roots to leaves?
questions.ex: Xylem vessels conduct water and dissolved minerals upward from roots to shoots.

questions.q: What kind of energy does a moving object have?
questions.ex: Kinetic energy is energy of motion possessed by moving objects.

questions.q: Which simple test shows a substance is acidic?
questions.ex: Acidic solutions turn blue litmus paper red.

questions.q: Which part of a seed develops into a new plant shoot?
questions.ex: The plumule is the embryonic shoot that grows upward to become the stem and leaves.

questions.q: A student observes that a plant's leaves are yellowing while veins remain green. What nutrient deficiency is most likely?
questions.ex: Interveinal chlorosis (yellowing between veins) with green veins is typical of iron deficiency.

questions.q: Which change shows a physical change rather than a chemical change?
questions.ex: Melting ice is a physical change; the chemical identity (water) remains the same.

questions.q: When a force acts on an object and it moves in the direction of the force, what has been done?
questions.ex: Work equals force multiplied by displacement in the direction of the force.

questions.q: Why do thicker wires have less electrical resistance than thinner wires of the same material?
options: They have more free electrons per length
They have larger cross-sectional area allowing easier flow
questions.ex: Larger cross-sectional area provides more paths for electrons, reducing resistance.

questions.q: A sealed container has gas and the temperature increases. What happens to pressure if volume stays constant?
questions.ex: At constant volume, increasing temperature raises gas molecule kinetic energy and pressure (Gay-Lussac's law).

questions.q: Which adaptation helps desert plants reduce water loss?
questions.ex: A thick waxy cuticle reduces transpiration and water loss in arid conditions.

questions.q: How does a teacher demonstrate that air has mass using simple classroom materials?
options: Weigh an empty and an inflated balloon
questions.ex: Weighing an empty and then an inflated balloon shows increased mass due to the air inside.

questions.q: Which of these correctly orders the levels of biological organization from smallest to larger?
questions.ex: Cells form tissues; tissues form organs; organs work in organ systems.

questions.q: A glass appears to have a coin visible when viewed from above due to refraction. Which property of light explains this?
questions.ex: Refraction (change of light direction when entering a medium) alters apparent position of objects in water or glass.

questions.q: Which human body system controls voluntary movement and communicates between body parts?
questions.ex: The nervous system sends signals to muscles for voluntary movement and coordinates body functions.

questions.q: Why are fertilizers used in agriculture?
options: To provide nutrients for plant growth
questions.ex: Fertilizers supply essential nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium for healthy plant growth.

questions.q: A teacher wants to show that sound needs a medium. Which demonstration is appropriate?
options: Playing music into a vacuum jar and observing pitch change
Placing ringing alarm inside evacuated jar; sound disappears
Using a tuning fork under water and hearing louder sound
questions.ex: Removing air from a jar prevents sound waves from traveling, demonstrating sound requires a medium.

questions.q: Which process reduces the number of chromosomes by half to produce gametes?
questions.ex: Meiosis produces gametes with half the chromosome number for sexual reproduction.

questions.q: Why does metal feel colder to touch than wood at the same temperature?
options: Metal conducts heat away from the hand faster
questions.ex: Metal has higher thermal conductivity, so it conducts heat away from your skin faster, making it feel colder.

questions.q: Which method separates a mixture of sand and salt where salt is soluble in water?
options: Dissolve and filter then evaporate water
questions.ex: Dissolve salt in water, filter to remove sand, then evaporate water to recover salt.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why leaves have stomata?
options: To allow gas exchange and transpiration
questions.ex: Stomata are pores that allow CO2 in for photosynthesis and release water vapor (transpiration).

questions.q: A student mixes vinegar and baking soda and observes bubbling and temperature change. What is produced?
questions.ex: Vinegar (acetic acid) reacts with baking soda (sodium bicarbonate) producing CO2 gas, water and usually a temperature change.

questions.q: Which factor most affects the period of a simple pendulum for small angles?
questions.ex: For small oscillations, a pendulum's period depends mainly on its length and gravity, not mass.

questions.q: Which classroom activity best shows that mixtures can be separated by density?
options: Mix sand and water and filter
Layer oil and colored water and observe separation
questions.ex: Liquids of different densities like oil and water naturally form layers, demonstrating density differences.

questions.q: How can teachers help students understand food chains in a local pond?
options: Show a single picture of a fish
Have students construct a food chain diagram including producers, consumers and decomposers
Tell students to memorize names of animals
questions.ex: Constructing diagrams with producers, consumers and decomposers helps students see energy flow and relationships.

questions.q: Why do incandescent bulbs convert less energy to light compared to fluorescent bulbs?
options: They emit more infrared (heat) wasting energy
questions.ex: Incandescent bulbs emit much energy as heat (infrared), making them less efficient at producing visible light than fluorescents.

questions.q: Which observation would indicate a chemical reaction has occurred in class?
options: Color change, gas formation, or temperature change
questions.ex: Chemical reactions often show color changes, gas production, temperature change, or formation of precipitate.

questions.q: A plant grown in darkness becomes tall and pale with small leaves. What process caused this?
options: Etiolation due to lack of light
questions.ex: Etiolation is the response to growing in low light: elongated stems and reduced chlorophyll (pale leaves).

questions.q: Which gas causes the greenhouse effect and is increased by burning fossil fuels?
questions.ex: Carbon dioxide is a major greenhouse gas whose atmospheric concentration rises with fossil fuel combustion.

questions.q: What is the main reason soils become salinized in irrigated fields?
questions.ex: When irrigation water evaporates, dissolved salts concentrate in the soil, causing salinization.

questions.q: Which of the following explains why a metal spoon heats faster in hot water than a wooden spoon?
options: Metal conducts heat better than wood
questions.ex: Metal's high thermal conductivity allows heat to travel quickly along the spoon; wood is an insulator.

questions.q: How can a teacher safely demonstrate static electricity in class?
options: Use wet hands to rub balloon on hair and stick to wall
Plug many devices into one socket
Allow students to touch a live wire
Burn paper to create smoke charges
questions.ex: Rubbing a balloon on hair transfers charge, making it cling to surfaces— a safe static electricity demo.

questions.q: Which observation supports that humans and plants have a symbiotic relationship?
options: Humans produce oxygen and plants produce carbon dioxide
Humans breathe in oxygen produced by plants and exhale carbon dioxide used by plants
Plants are harmed by human respiration
questions.ex: Humans use plant-produced oxygen; plants use human-exhaled carbon dioxide, showing mutual dependence.

questions.q: During a lab, students notice that adding salt to water increases its boiling point slightly. What is this effect called?
questions.ex: Adding a non-volatile solute like salt raises the boiling point of water; this is boiling point elevation.

questions.q: Why are wetlands important in the environment?
options: They act as natural water filters and habitats
questions.ex: Wetlands filter pollutants, store floodwater, and provide habitats, supporting biodiversity and water quality.

questions.q: A teacher mixes equal masses of two liquids: one volatile with low boiling point and one non-volatile. After evaporating the mixture gently, which remains and why?
options: Volatile liquid remains because it has low boiling point
Non-volatile solute remains because volatile component evaporates first
questions.ex: The volatile liquid evaporates first on gentle heating, leaving behind the non-volatile substance or solute.

questions.q: In planning a lesson on plant transpiration, which classroom test best isolates the role of stomata?
options: Measure weight loss of whole potted plant in light vs dark
Cover leaves with oil and compare water loss to uncovered leaves
Cut roots and observe wilting speed
Place plants in different soil types
questions.ex: Coating stomata with oil prevents gas exchange; comparing coated vs uncoated leaves isolates stomatal transpiration.

questions.q: A student draws a circuit with two identical bulbs in series connected to a battery. If one bulb burns out, what happens to the other and why?
options: Other bulb gets brighter because current increases
Other bulb remains same because parallel effect
Other bulb goes out because series circuit current stops
Other bulb flickers due to capacitance
questions.ex: In a series circuit current flows through each component; if one bulb breaks, the circuit opens and current stops, so both go out.

questions.q: How would you explain to students why sound’s speed is greater in solids than in gases?
options: Solids are denser so waves slow down
Particles in solids are closer, enabling faster vibration transfer
questions.ex: Closer particle spacing and stronger elastic forces in solids allow mechanical vibrations (sound) to propagate faster than in gases.

questions.q: During meiosis, a teacher asks why genetic variation occurs. Which mechanism should be emphasized?
questions.ex: Independent assortment of homologues and crossing over during meiosis create new allele combinations, increasing variation.

questions.q: A soil sample test shows poor nitrogen but high phosphorus. Which management practice would best address crop nitrogen needs sustainably?
questions.ex: Legume rotation introduces symbiotic nitrogen-fixing bacteria, improving soil nitrogen sustainably without excess chemical fertilizer.

questions.q: A demonstration uses two identical metal rods, one heated and one at room temperature, then placed in oil; the heated rod floats lower. What concept explains this?
options: Thermal expansion reduces density causing more displacement
Heat creates buoyant force independent of density
questions.ex: Heating expands the rod increasing its volume while mass remains same, lowering density so it displaces more oil and floats lower.

questions.q: A teacher tests plant growth under colored lights. Plants under green light grow poorly. Why?
options: Green light is absorbed most by chlorophyll
Green light is reflected by leaves and not available for photosynthesis
Green light provides more energy than red
questions.ex: Leaves reflect green wavelengths; less green light is absorbed by chlorophyll for photosynthesis, resulting in poorer growth.

questions.q: When comparing combustion of wood and methane, which statement about energy release per unit mass is generally true?
options: Wood releases more energy per mass than methane
Methane releases more energy per mass than wood
Both release identical energy per mass
Energy release depends only on oxygen availability not fuel
questions.ex: Methane, a hydrocarbon gas, typically releases more energy per kilogram when combusted compared to wood, which contains moisture and ash.

questions.q: A pupil asks why oceans appear blue. Which explanation is most correct and classroom-appropriate?
options: Oceans are blue because they reflect the sky only
Water molecules absorb longer wavelengths (red) more, scattering blue
Blue dye in water causes color
questions.ex: Water absorbs longer wavelengths (red) more strongly; shorter blue wavelengths are preferentially scattered and transmitted, giving a blue appearance.

questions.q: In ecology, why might introducing a non-native predator reduce biodiversity?
options: It may prey on native species with no evolved defenses, causing extinctions
questions.ex: Non-native predators can decimate native populations that lack adaptations, leading to reduced biodiversity and ecosystem imbalance.

questions.q: A lab question: students determined the density of an irregular object using water displacement; their volume measurements varied slightly. Which technique improves precision?
options: Use a larger overflow container and repeated trials
questions.ex: Larger container reduces relative error, and repeating trials allows averaging to improve precision in water displacement measurements.

questions.q: A teacher shows planetary orbits are elliptical. Which classroom activity best demonstrates this?
options: Stretch a string between two pins and move a pencil with a loop to trace ellipse
Roll a ball in a circular path
Use only a compass to draw circles
questions.ex: The two-pin-and-string method physically traces an ellipse, illustrating how ellipses differ from circles in a hands-on way.

questions.q: During a lab, an acid is gradually added to a carbonate until fizzing stops. Which measurement best indicates reaction completion?
options: pH stabilization and absence of CO2 bubbles
questions.ex: The reaction produces CO2; when bubbling stops and pH no longer changes, the carbonate has been consumed indicating completion.

questions.q: A student asks how to reduce measurement error when timing pendulum swings. Which practice helps most?
options: Use stopwatch and time one swing
Start and stop at arbitrary points
Time many oscillations and divide by number of swings
questions.ex: Timing many oscillations reduces random reaction-time error; dividing total time by number of swings yields a more accurate period.

questions.q: How should a teacher address students' misconception that heavier objects fall faster?
options: Demonstrate dropping two objects of different masses in air and observe
Show video of feather and coin in vacuum and in air to illustrate effect of air resistance vs mass
Tell them the heavier is always faster
questions.ex: Using demonstrations in air and vacuum shows that in absence of air resistance, objects fall at same acceleration regardless of mass; in air, resistance causes differences.

questions.q: Which soil management practice best prevents erosion on sloped farmland?
options: Plowing up and down the slope
questions.ex: Contour farming and terracing reduce runoff speed and soil loss on slopes, effectively preventing erosion.

questions.q: A child asks why ice floats. Which classroom explanation is accurate and age-appropriate?
options: Ice has more mass than water
Ice is less dense than liquid water because its crystalline structure holds more space
Ice turns into gas under pressure
questions.ex: Water expands on freezing forming a lattice that occupies more volume, so ice has lower density than liquid water and floats.

questions.q: Which pedagogical approach best helps students distinguish between mixture and compound?
options: Hands-on activities where students mix substances and test separation methods
questions.ex: Hands-on experiments (e.g., salt + sand vs salt + water) allow students to observe separability and properties, clarifying mixture vs compound.

questions.q: A class measures light intensity at different distances from a bulb. Which relationship should students expect?
options: Intensity increases with square of distance
Intensity decreases with the square of distance (inverse square law)
questions.ex: For a point-like source, intensity spreads over a sphere and decreases proportional to 1/d^2 (inverse square law).

questions.q: A question on nutrition: which deficiency is most likely to cause weak bones and rickets in children?
questions.ex: Vitamin D is necessary for calcium absorption and bone mineralization; deficiency in children can cause rickets.

questions.q: During a unit on renewable energy, students compare hydroelectric and solar power. Which classroom metric best compares their capacity to generate electricity consistently?
questions.ex: Capacity factor measures actual electricity generated over time relative to maximum possible, reflecting consistency and reliability.

questions.q: A chemistry question: why does adding an inert gas at constant temperature increase total pressure in a fixed-volume container but not partial pressures of reactive gases?
options: Inert gas reacts and removes others
Total pressure rises because of added gas molecules; partial pressures of existing gases remain unchanged at same temperature and volume (Dalton's law)
questions.ex: Dalton's law: total pressure equals sum of partial pressures; adding inert gas increases total pressure but does not change partial pressures of gases if temperature and volume stay constant.

questions.q: How can teachers assess understanding of adaptation vs acclimatization in animals?
options: Ask students to memorize definitions only
Use case studies: compare long-term evolutionary traits (adaptations) vs short-term physiological changes (acclimatization)
Ignore examples and discuss genetics only
questions.ex: Case studies contrasting inherited traits across generations with short-term physiological adjustments help students distinguish adaptation from acclimatization.

questions.q: A lab shows a metal salt solution changing color when electricity is passed through it. What process is occurring at the electrode?
options: Electrolysis causing redox reactions and deposition of metals
questions.ex: Electrolysis drives oxidation-reduction at electrodes, causing metal ions to be reduced and deposit or coloration changes due to oxidation states.

questions.q: Which classroom strategy helps students grasp scale differences between Earth and other planets?
options: Using exact models to scale of planet sizes and distances on paper
Placing planet models at true relative distances in a classroom-sized scale model (logarithmic or scaled distances)
questions.ex: Scaled models with adjusted distances (often logarithmic for practicality) help learners visualize relative sizes and separations more effectively than numbers alone.

questions.q: In an experiment measuring rate of photosynthesis, which variable should be changed to test light intensity effect while controlling others?
options: Change CO2 concentration and light together
Vary light intensity while keeping CO2, temperature and water constant
questions.ex: To isolate light intensity's effect, keep CO2, temperature and water constant so observed changes are attributable to light changes.

questions.q: A question on floods: which integrated classroom activity best teaches flood mitigation for a riverside village?
options: Have students design a model village with flood defenses like levees, early-warning systems and land-use planning and simulate heavy rain
Ask students to write essays only
Demonstrate a single sandbag technique without context
questions.ex: Designing models and simulating scenarios engages students in multiple mitigation strategies (structural and non-structural) and systems thinking.

questions.q: A student wonders why a comet has a tail pointing away from the Sun regardless of its direction of motion. What causes this?
options: Solar radiation and solar wind push gas and dust away from the comet, making tails point away from the Sun
Comet tail aligns with planet's magnetic field
Gravitational pull of planets forms tail
questions.ex: Solar radiation pressure and the solar wind exert forces that push the comet's gas and dust away from the Sun, so the tail points away.

questions.q: In teaching about infectious diseases, which classroom activity best conveys how vaccines work?
options: Explain that vaccines are medicines that cure disease
Use role-play showing immune system memory where a harmless antigen exposure leads to faster future response
Show only graphs of case numbers
questions.ex: Role-play or models illustrating how vaccination creates immune memory and faster secondary responses helps students understand vaccine function without technical complexity.

questions.q: Which is the capital city of Pakistan?
questions.ex: Islamabad is the capital city and seat of government of Pakistan.

questions.q: What is the national language of Pakistan?
questions.ex: Urdu is the national language used for communication across Pakistan.

questions.q: Which river flows through Sindh province and is vital for its agriculture?
questions.ex: The Indus River flows through Sindh and supports irrigation and farming.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of a map?
questions.ex: Maps are used to show locations, physical features, and spatial relationships.

questions.q: Which of these is a major language spoken in Sindh?
questions.ex: Sindhi is the main regional language spoken by the people of Sindh.

questions.q: What festival is celebrated as Pakistan’s Independence Day?
questions.ex: 14 August marks Pakistan's Independence Day, celebrated nationwide.

questions.q: Who is the head of a village government in the local system often called in rural Sindh?
questions.ex: A village head or similar local leader (often called sarpanch/numberdar) leads local rural governance.

questions.q: Which crop is commonly grown in Sindh due to irrigation from the Indus?
questions.ex: Wheat is a common irrigated crop in Sindh supported by canal systems from the Indus.

questions.q: What does a citizen's duty include?
questions.ex: Citizens have duties such as obeying laws, paying taxes, and participating in civic life.

questions.q: Which of these is part of natural environment?
questions.ex: A river is a natural feature of the environment.

questions.q: What is the first thing to do in an earthquake to stay safe?
questions.ex: During an earthquake, drop, cover and hold on to protect yourself from falling objects.

questions.q: Which animal is commonly associated with Sindh’s culture and rural life?
questions.ex: Camels are commonly used and culturally linked to rural life in parts of Sindh.

questions.q: What do we call a group of people who live in the same area and follow rules?
questions.ex: A community is a group of people living together who share rules and relationships.

questions.q: Which sea borders Sindh to the south?
questions.ex: The Arabian Sea lies to the south of Sindh province.

questions.q: What is the main reason for building canals in Sindh?
questions.ex: Canals distribute water from rivers to fields for irrigation and farming.

questions.q: Which action shows good citizenship in school?
questions.ex: Helping classmates shows responsibility, respect and cooperation—qualities of good citizenship.

questions.q: What is the name of the long, traditional Sindhi hat often worn during cultural events?
questions.ex: The Sindhi topi is a traditional cap worn in Sindh, especially during cultural occasions.

questions.q: Which season brings monsoon rains important for crops in parts of Pakistan?
questions.ex: The monsoon season in summer brings important rains vital for agriculture in many regions.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a ballot during elections?
questions.ex: A ballot is used by citizens to cast their vote for chosen candidates in elections.

questions.q: Which energy source is renewable?
questions.ex: Wind is a renewable energy source that can be naturally replenished.

questions.q: Which historical city in Sindh was an important center of the Indus Valley Civilization?
questions.ex: Mohenjo-daro in Sindh was a major urban center of the ancient Indus Valley Civilization.

questions.q: What tool helps students read distances and directions on a map?
questions.ex: A compass shows direction and a scale helps measure distances on a map.

questions.q: Which right allows citizens to choose their leaders?
questions.ex: The right to vote enables citizens to participate in choosing their government leaders.

questions.q: Which food product is Sindh known for producing?
questions.ex: Sindh produces crops like rice, especially in irrigated areas.

questions.q: What is the correct behavior during a flood warning?
options: Wait for instructions and move to higher ground
questions.ex: During flood warnings people should move to safe, higher ground and follow authorities' instructions.

questions.q: Which institution in a town resolves local disputes and provides civic services?
questions.ex: Local governments or municipalities handle services like water, roads and local dispute resolution.

questions.q: Why are trees important for the environment?
questions.ex: Trees produce oxygen, offer shade, prevent soil erosion and support biodiversity.

questions.q: Which form of transport is commonly used to move goods along the Indus plains?
questions.ex: Boats (in some areas) and trucks are commonly used to transport goods across the plains and along waterways.

questions.q: What does 'culture' include?
questions.ex: Culture includes beliefs, customs, language, arts and social practices of a group.

questions.q: Which governmental level makes laws for the whole country?
questions.ex: The National Parliament (federal government) makes laws that apply to the entire country.

questions.q: A student is making a simple map of their village. Which symbol should they use to show a school?
options: A book or small building symbol
questions.ex: A school is best represented by a building or book symbol to clearly indicate an educational institution.

questions.q: Which practice helps conserve water in agriculture in Sindh?
questions.ex: Drip irrigation delivers water efficiently to roots, conserving water compared with flood irrigation.

questions.q: How can teachers encourage good citizenship in primary students?
options: By teaching responsibilities, respect and helping others
questions.ex: Teaching responsibilities, respect and community service fosters civic awareness and good citizenship.

questions.q: Which economic activity is most likely to support coastal communities in Sindh?
questions.ex: Coastal communities often depend on fishing and port-related trade for livelihood.

questions.q: If a village near the Indus is at risk of salinity in soil, what is a practical measure farmers can take?
questions.ex: Improving drainage and crop rotation can reduce soil salinity and maintain productivity.

questions.q: Which civic process allows citizens to express disagreement with a local decision?
questions.ex: Citizens can use petitions and public meetings to peacefully and formally express concerns.

questions.q: A teacher explains seasons to students in Sindh. Which cause should be included?
options: Changes in Earth's distance from the sun only
Tilt of Earth's axis causing varying sun angle
questions.ex: Seasons result from Earth's axial tilt, changing the sun's angle and daylight, not distance to the sun alone.

questions.q: Why is Mohenjo-daro important to social studies in Sindh classrooms?
options: It provides evidence of ancient urban planning and crafts
questions.ex: Mohenjo-daro illustrates advanced urban planning, social organization and craft skills of the Indus Valley Civilization.

questions.q: Which method is best for teaching primary students about local government functions?
options: Field visit to municipal office or inviting local official
questions.ex: Field visits or guest speakers make local government functions concrete and engaging for young learners.

questions.q: How can schools in Sindh reduce their environmental footprint?
options: Starting tree-planting, waste segregation and water-saving measures
questions.ex: Tree planting, waste segregation and water-saving are practical school actions to lower environmental impact.

questions.q: A map shows contour lines close together in a part of Sindh. What does this indicate?
questions.ex: Close contour lines on a map indicate a steep slope or rapid elevation change.

questions.q: Which source would be most reliable for teaching historical facts about Sindh to Grade 6 students?
options: An archaeological report or reputable history book
questions.ex: Archaeological reports and scholarly history books provide verified, reliable information for classroom teaching.

questions.q: What is an effect of urbanization in Sindh's major cities like Karachi?
options: Pressure on housing, services and environment
questions.ex: Urbanization increases demand for housing, infrastructure and services, straining resources and environments.

questions.q: If a teacher wants to assess students' understanding of civic rights, which activity is most appropriate?
options: Role-play of voting and discussing rights
questions.ex: Role-play helps students practice and internalize the concept of voting and civic rights actively.

questions.q: Which practice would help protect the Indus River ecosystem?
questions.ex: Treating wastewater and controlling pollution help protect river ecosystems and biodiversity.

questions.q: How can teachers integrate local culture into social studies lessons?
options: Use local stories, songs, crafts and field visits
questions.ex: Using local culture and visiting cultural sites makes lessons relevant and meaningful to students.

questions.q: Which feature distinguishes a democracy from other systems?
options: Citizens participate in choosing leaders through elections
questions.ex: Democracy is characterized by citizens' participation in electing leaders through fair elections.

questions.q: A class project asks students to compare rural and urban livelihoods in Sindh. Which method yields best results?
options: Collecting interviews, observations and photos from both areas
questions.ex: Field observations, interviews and photos provide concrete evidence for comparing livelihoods.

questions.q: Which tool would help measure rainfall in a school science corner?
questions.ex: A rain gauge measures the amount of rainfall collected over a period.

questions.q: Why is preserving languages like Sindhi important in schools?
options: It helps maintain cultural identity and communication
questions.ex: Teaching local languages sustains cultural heritage and helps students connect with their community.

questions.q: Which economic policy would most directly support small farmers in Sindh?
options: Removing subsidies for seeds and fertilizers
Providing access to credit, extension services and fair markets
questions.ex: Access to credit, training and markets helps small farmers invest, improve yields and sell produce.

questions.q: In teaching about ancient crafts, which classroom activity best supports skill understanding?
options: Hands-on craft demonstrations and museum visits
questions.ex: Hands-on demonstrations and museum visits help students understand techniques and cultural contexts of crafts.

questions.q: Which statement about citizenship education is most suitable for Grade 4?
options: Citizens must always agree with government
Citizens have rights and responsibilities and can participate peacefully
questions.ex: Grade 4 students should learn that citizenship includes rights, responsibilities, and peaceful participation.

questions.q: How should teachers handle sensitive historical topics in middle school?
options: Present balanced, age-appropriate facts and encourage critical thinking
questions.ex: Balanced, age-appropriate presentation with critical discussion helps students understand complex history responsibly.

questions.q: What is a likely consequence of overuse of groundwater in Sindh?
options: Lowering of water table and increased salinity
questions.ex: Excessive groundwater extraction can lower water tables and cause salinity and land subsidence.

questions.q: Which approach helps students learn map reading faster?
options: Interactive map activities with compass and scale practice
questions.ex: Interactive practice with real maps and tools improves students' map-reading skills effectively.

questions.q: Why teach students about trade and markets in social studies?
options: To show how people exchange goods, earn livelihoods and depend on markets
questions.ex: Teaching about trade explains how people obtain goods, earn incomes, and how markets affect daily life.

questions.q: Which classroom assessment best measures students' understanding of local history?
options: Project-based assessment with timelines and presentations
questions.ex: Project-based assessments allow students to research, organize and present historical understanding creatively.

questions.q: Which human activity most increases flood risk in urban areas?
options: Removing natural drainage and covering wetlands
questions.ex: Destroying natural drainage and wetlands increases runoff and heightens flood risk in urban areas.

questions.q: How can schools help preserve local heritage sites?
options: Organize student awareness programs and community clean-ups
questions.ex: Awareness activities and community participation engage students in protecting heritage sites.

questions.q: A Grade 7 teacher plans a lesson linking Indus Valley urban planning to modern city planning. Which analytical activity best develops students’ higher-order thinking?
options: Ask students to compare street grids, drainage systems and public spaces then propose improvements for a local neighborhood
Tell students that ancient cities are irrelevant
questions.ex: Comparing ancient and modern systems and proposing improvements engages analysis, synthesis and application.

questions.q: A village near a canal experiences seasonal waterlogging and declining crop yields. As a teacher advising a community project, which integrated solution is most appropriate?
options: Recommend improving drainage, crop rotation, and community-managed water schedules
questions.ex: Integrated measures—drainage improvement, crop rotation and cooperative water management—address waterlogging and sustain agriculture.

questions.q: While teaching about citizenship, a student asks about corruption’s impact on families. Which classroom approach is best?
options: Facilitate a guided discussion on effects of corruption on services, and ways citizens can promote transparency
questions.ex: A guided discussion helps students critically understand real-life impacts and constructive civic responses.

questions.q: You observe a Grade 6 lesson where students memorize facts about Mohenjo-daro. How can you redesign the task to foster inquiry?
options: Assign students to investigate household artifacts' uses and present hypotheses backed by evidence
questions.ex: Investigating artifacts and forming evidence-based hypotheses encourages inquiry and critical thinking.

questions.q: A map activity shows shrinking wetland areas near a Sindh estuary. Which classroom project helps students analyze causes and propose mitigation?
options: Research land use changes, interview locals, measure water quality and propose protection plans
questions.ex: Combining research, local interviews and data collection enables students to analyze causes and suggest practical mitigation.

questions.q: A middle-school class needs to evaluate the economic effects of a new highway in Sindh. Which assessment gives the most balanced analysis?
options: Conduct a cost-benefit study including livelihoods, environment, access, and displacement effects
questions.ex: A cost-benefit approach considers multiple economic, social and environmental impacts for balanced evaluation.

questions.q: When teaching about climate impacts, students note increased salinity in coastal groundwater. Which scientific classroom investigation is most appropriate?
options: Test salinity at different distances from coast, analyze land use changes and discuss adaptation strategies
questions.ex: Measuring salinity gradients and linking them to land use helps students understand local climate impacts and adaptation.

questions.q: A teacher wants to assess deeper understanding of local governance. Which project aligns with curriculum standards for middle grades?
options: Organize mock local council where students research issues, hold hearings and recommend policies
questions.ex: Mock councils with research and hearings develop civic skills, policy understanding and decision-making.

questions.q: In a unit on cultural diversity, how should a teacher handle differing community narratives about a historical event?
options: Present multiple sources, discuss perspective and encourage respectful comparison
questions.ex: Presenting multiple sources and discussing perspectives teaches critical thinking and respect for diverse views.

questions.q: A school near Karachi faces waste management issues. Which interdisciplinary student project best addresses both social and environmental aspects?
options: Survey waste sources, analyze collection systems, propose community-based recycling and awareness campaigns
questions.ex: A project combining survey, systems analysis and community proposals connects social behavior with environmental solutions.

questions.q: During a unit on trade, students must analyze how Sindh’s ports affect inland farmers. Which inquiry question is most productive?
options: How do port fees, transport costs and market access affect farmers’ prices and income?
questions.ex: Analyzing fees, transport and market access helps students explore the economic linkages between ports and farming communities.

questions.q: A teacher notices students stereotype rural people as uneducated. Which classroom intervention best promotes balanced understanding?
options: Design a study where students interview rural role models, document skills and present findings to challenge assumptions
questions.ex: Interviewing and documenting real-life rural skills provides evidence to counter stereotypes and build nuanced views.

questions.q: You must design an assessment for Grade 8 on environmental policy. Which task best measures analytical and evaluative skills?
options: Ask students to evaluate a local water management policy, identify strengths/weaknesses and recommend improvements with justification
Have students draw a map only
questions.ex: Evaluating policy with justification requires analysis, application of knowledge and reasoned recommendations.

questions.q: A teacher uses a historical source that may be biased. What is the best classroom practice?
options: Teach source criticism: author, purpose, audience and cross-check with other evidence
Insist students accept it as truth
questions.ex: Teaching source criticism helps students assess reliability and understand historical perspectives.

questions.q: While teaching natural hazards, students ask why poorer communities are more vulnerable. How should this be addressed pedagogically?
options: Discuss factors like housing quality, resource access, and propose equitable mitigation policies
questions.ex: Discussing socioeconomic factors and equitable policies fosters understanding of vulnerability and justice issues.

questions.q: A student research group wants to study migration patterns from rural Sindh to cities. Which mixed-method approach is most appropriate?
options: Combine household surveys, interviews, and analysis of economic opportunities and urban services
questions.ex: Mixed methods (surveys, interviews and economic analysis) provide comprehensive insights into migration drivers and effects.

questions.q: In a lesson on resources, students are to prioritize sustainable use choices. Which classroom rubric best assesses their reasoning?
options: Criteria including environmental impact, economic feasibility, social equity and long-term sustainability
questions.ex: A rubric that values environmental, economic and social criteria assesses the quality of students' sustainability reasoning.

questions.q: A Grade 7 civics unit examines voter turnout decline. Which classroom experiment would yield meaningful conclusions?
options: Analyze past turnout data, survey local voters about barriers, and propose targeted interventions
questions.ex: Data analysis combined with local surveys helps identify causes and design evidence-based interventions.

questions.q: When discussing Indus River basin management, which allocation principle balances needs of irrigation, ecology and cities?
options: Integrated water resources management considering ecological flows, equitable irrigation and urban supply
questions.ex: Integrated water resources management seeks balanced allocation across ecological, agricultural and urban needs.

questions.q: A student claims that all cultural change is negative. How should a teacher facilitate a critical discussion?
options: Guide students to cite examples of positive and negative changes and analyze causes and consequences
questions.ex: Examining examples and analyzing impacts encourages nuanced critical thinking about cultural change.

questions.q: Which classroom assessment best measures understanding of causes of soil salinity in Sindh?
options: Require a cause-effect diagram showing irrigation practices, waterlogging, and suggestions for remediation
questions.ex: A cause-effect diagram demonstrates students' grasp of interrelated factors and potential remediation measures.

questions.q: A teacher must present controversial land-use case in which industrial development threatens an archaeological site. What is the best pedagogical plan?
options: Present stakeholders' perspectives, legal protections, economic arguments and facilitate a reasoned class debate
questions.ex: Presenting multiple perspectives and facilitating debate develops critical thinking and understanding of complex trade-offs.

questions.q: How can teachers incorporate gender perspectives into lessons on local economy without stereotyping?
options: Use data showing gendered roles, discuss barriers and include examples of diverse contributions and solutions
questions.ex: Using data, discussing barriers and showcasing diverse roles promotes inclusive understanding without stereotyping.

questions.q: A school plans to restore a nearby wetland as a service-learning project. Which evaluation metric best measures ecological and social outcomes?
options: Biodiversity indices, water quality measures, and community usage and attitudes before and after the project
Only celebrate the effort without measuring outcomes
questions.ex: Combining ecological indicators and community feedback measures both environmental and social impacts of restoration.
