questions.q: While teaching map scales, a student asks how distortions occur in flat maps of the Earth. Which explanation and classroom activity is most effective?
options: Explain projection issues and have students compare distances on different map projections and globe measurements
Tell them to use only atlases
questions.ex: Explaining map projections and comparing multiple projections with a globe illustrates why distortions occur.

questions.q: A curriculum reviewer asks for a Grade 8 unit linking environment and economy in Sindh’s delta. What essential question best frames inquiry?
options: How can the Sindh delta sustain livelihoods while protecting ecosystems?
questions.ex: This essential question focuses inquiry on balancing livelihoods and ecological protection—central to sustainable development.

questions.q: A teacher observes students accepting an oversimplified cause for the decline of an ancient city. Which strategy deepens their historical analysis?
options: Let them stay with the simplification
Introduce multiple evidence types (archaeological, climatic, trade) and have students weigh competing explanations
questions.ex: Weighing multiple evidence types encourages complex causal analysis and critical evaluation of historical explanations.

questions.q: In designing a case study on coastal erosion in Sindh, which student task best integrates data literacy and civic engagement?
options: Collect shoreline measurements, interview affected households, map changes over time and propose community advocacy strategies
questions.ex: Combining measurement, interviews, mapping and advocacy links data analysis with practical civic action.

questions.q: A teacher wants to assess student mastery of migration’s social causes. Which summative task is most rigorous?
options: Analytical essay using local data and interviews to argue which factors (economic, environmental, social) were most influential
questions.ex: An essay requiring local data and interviews demands synthesis, evidence use and critical argumentation.

questions.q: Which classroom activity best helps students evaluate competing land-right claims between farmers and developers?
options: Hold a simulated mediation where students represent stakeholders, use maps, laws and economic data to negotiate
questions.ex: Simulated mediation engages students in using spatial data, laws and economic arguments to negotiate real-world conflicts.

questions.q: درست واحد شکل منتخب کریں: 'کتابیں' کا واحد کیا ہے؟
questions.ex: کتابیں جمع کا واحد لفظ 'کتاب' ہے۔

questions.q: مذکر لفظ کون سا ہے؟ 'لڑکا' ، 'لڑکی' ، 'گھڑی' ، 'میز'
questions.ex: 'لڑکا' واضح طور پر مذکر ہے؛ باقی الفاظ میں 'لڑکی' مونث ہے، 'گھڑی' اور 'میز' عام طور پر مونث معنوں میں آتے ہیں۔

questions.q: درست مترادف جوڑی منتخب کریں: 'خوش'
questions.ex: 'خوش' کا مترادف 'خوشحال' ہے؛ باقی الفاظ مختلف معنی رکھتے ہیں۔

questions.q: درست متضاد لفظ منتخب کریں: 'تیز'
questions.ex: 'تیز' کا متضاد 'آہستہ' ہے۔

questions.q: درست جملہ منتخب کریں:
questions.ex: اگر فاعل 'وہ' (مونث) مراد ہو تو 'وہ بازار گئی۔' درست جملہ ہے۔

questions.q: 'کہانی' کا جمع کیا ہوگا؟
questions.ex: 'کہانی' کی جمع 'کہانیاں' بنتی ہے۔

questions.q: صحیح لفظ منتخب کریں: 'میں __ کتاب پڑھ رہا ہوں.'
questions.ex: عام اردو میں 'ایک' درست شمار لفظ ہے: 'میں ایک کتاب پڑھ رہا ہوں۔'

questions.q: مناسب ضمیر کا انتخاب کریں: 'علی نے اپنا کام کیا۔ __ خوش تھا.'
questions.ex: جملہ علی کے بارے میں ہے، اس لیے 'وہ' مناسب ضمیر ہے۔

questions.q: ہجے درست کریں: 'استاد' کا صحیح ہجے کیا ہے؟
questions.ex: صحیح ہجے 'استاد' ہے۔

questions.q: یہ کون سا لفظ ہے؟ 'بڑی' — یہ ____ ہے۔
questions.ex: 'بڑی' چیز کی وصف بتاتی ہے، اس لیے یہ 'صفت' ہے۔

questions.q: صحیح فعل کا انتخاب کریں: 'وہ روز اسکول __ جاتا ہے.'
questions.ex: جملہ 'وہ روز اسکول بھی جاتا ہے۔' درست بنتا ہے؛ 'بھی' مناسب حرفِ ربط ہے۔

questions.q: درست اردو ماننے والا لفظ: 'apple' کا عام اردو لفظ کیا ہے؟
questions.ex: انگریزی 'apple' کا اردو میں عام ترجمہ 'سیب' ہے۔

questions.q: مناسب جمع بنائیں: 'پھول' کا جمع کیا ہے؟
questions.ex: فقرہ میں 'پھول' کا جمع عام طور پر 'پھول' یا 'پھولوں' استعمال ہوتا ہے؛ بطور جمع اسم کے لیے 'پھول' بھی آتا ہے مگر سوال کے سیاق میں 'پھولوں' درست جمع کی شکل ہے۔

questions.q: صحیح ماضی کا فعل منتخب کریں: 'وہ کل اسکول __.'
questions.ex: ماضی میں ہونے والا عمل 'گیا' کے ساتھ درست ہوتا ہے: 'وہ کل اسکول گیا۔'

questions.q: کون سا لفظ ضمیر ہے؟
questions.ex: 'ہم' ایک شخصی ضمیر ہے؛ باقی مختلف اقسام کے الفاظ ہیں۔

questions.q: مناسب مرادف منتخب کریں: 'پینا'
questions.ex: 'پینا' کا مترادف بول چال میں 'نالینا' نہیں عام ہے مگر یہاں درست جواب 'نالینا' نہیں مناسب؛ تاہم سب opties کے اندر 'نالینا' قریبی تہذیبی لفظ ہے۔

questions.q: صحیح حکم جملہ منتخب کریں: 'دروازہ __ .'
questions.ex: آمری شکل 'بند کرو' عام طور پر واحد مخاطب کے لیے درست حکم ہے۔

questions.q: جملہ درست کریں: 'میں اسکول جاتا ہوں.' (لڑکی بول رہی ہو)
questions.ex: اگر بولنے والی لڑکی ہو تو 'میں اسکول جاتی ہوں۔' چاہئے۔

questions.q: 'ماں' کا متضاد لفظ کون سا ہے؟
questions.ex: 'ماں' کا منطقی متضاد 'باپ' ہے (خاندانی رشتہ میں)۔

questions.q: محاورہ پہچانیں: 'آنکھ کا تارا' کا مطلب کیا؟
questions.ex: 'آنکھ کا تارا' کا مطلب کسی کو بہت عزیز یا پسندیدہ ہونا ہے۔

questions.q: کیا یہ جملہ درست ہے؟ 'وہ دوڑتی.'
questions.ex: جملہ 'وہ دوڑتی۔' اگر مونث فاعل ہو تو مختصر درست جملہ ہے۔

questions.q: صحیح حرفِ جار منتخب کریں: '______ اسکول.'
questions.ex: سوال غالباً 'میں اسکول' کے سیاق کا ہے؛ 'میں' مناسب ہے۔

questions.q: سیدھا سوال بنائیں: 'وہ کہاں ہے؟' کا جواب چاہیے: 'وہ __ ہے.'
questions.ex: مکمل جواب 'وہ گھر میں ہے۔' درست فقرہ ہے۔

questions.q: مناسب فعل تلاش کریں: 'بچے کھیل _____ .'
questions.ex: جمع 'بچے' کے ساتھ 'رہے' استعمال ہوتا ہے: 'بچے کھیل رہے۔'

questions.q: صحیح لفظ چنیں: 'صبح کا وقت' — 'صبح' کی لغوی قسم کیا ہے؟
questions.ex: 'صبح' ایک زمانہ/وقت بتانے والا اسم ہے۔

questions.q: کیا یہ لفظ جمع ہے یا واحد: 'لوگ'؟
questions.ex: 'لوگ' عام طور پر جمع اسم ہے۔

questions.q: جملہ میں صحیح حرفِ ربط: 'میں بازار ____ گیا.'
questions.ex: عام جملے میں 'میں بازار کو گیا' کم عام؛ بہتر 'میں بازار گیا' یا 'میں بازار کو گیا' دونوں اگرچہ 'کو' مفعولی نیت ظاہر کرتا ہے۔

questions.q: 'اچھا' کا مذکر اور مونث — مونث صورت کیا ہے؟
questions.ex: صفت 'اچھا' کی مونث شکل 'اچھی' ہے۔

questions.q: لفظ کی درجہ بندی: 'دودھ' کس قسم کا لفظ ہے؟
questions.ex: 'دودھ' ایک شے/غذا ہے، اس لیے اسم ہے۔

questions.q: صحیح تلفظ یا ہجے کا انتخاب: 'خوراک' کا درست ہجے؟
questions.ex: عام اردو ہجے 'خوراک' ہے۔

questions.q: جملے میں درست ترتیب منتخب کریں: 'اس نے کتاب میز پر رکھی.' بہتر ترتیب کیا ہوگی؟
options: اس نے کتاب میز پر رکھی.
اس نے میز پر کتاب رکھی.
کتاب اس نے میز پر رکھی.
میز پر کتاب اس نے رکھی.
questions.ex: عام فصیح ترتیب 'اس نے میز پر کتاب رکھی۔' ہے جو زیادہ فطری معلوم ہوتی ہے۔

questions.q: مناسب مترادف جوڑا منتخب کریں: 'دکھ'
questions.ex: 'دکھ' کا مترادف 'غم' ہے؛ باقی الفاظ مخالف یا الگ معنی دیتے ہیں۔

questions.q: کون سا جملہ نحوی طور پر درست ہے؟
options: میں نے کل ایک خط لکھا۔
میں نے کل ایک خط لکھیں۔
میں نے لکھا کل ایک خط۔
questions.ex: صحیح مرکب فعل اور ماضی کے ساتھ 'میں نے کل ایک خط لکھا۔' درست ہے۔

questions.q: جملہ درست کریں (گرامر): 'ہم کل بازار گئی۔'
questions.ex: 'ہم' جمع مذکر/مختلط صورت میں 'گئے' استعمال ہوتا ہے: 'ہم کل بازار گئے۔' اگر تمام مرد ہوں۔ کلاس میں عمومی درستگی کے لیے 'گئے' درست ہے۔

questions.q: درست متضاد لفظ کون سا ہے: 'صاف'؟
questions.ex: 'صاف' کا متضاد 'گندہ' ہے۔

questions.q: محاورہ سمجھیں: 'نیکی کر دریا میں ڈال' کا مطلب کیا ہے؟
questions.ex: محاورہ کا مطلب ہے نیکی کرو بغیر دکھاوے کے، یعنی نیکی کو چھپانا۔

questions.q: مناسب پرسونا پر مبنی ترمیم: 'آپ کل اسکول ____ ہیں؟' (سوال بطور شائستہ)
questions.ex: 'آپ' کے لیے شائستہ شکل 'جاتے' استعمال ہوتی ہے: 'آپ کل اسکول جاتے ہیں؟'

questions.q: ادبی علم: نظم میں استعارہ کیا کرتا ہے؟
options: ایک چیز کو دوسری کی مانند بتاتا ہے
questions.ex: استعارہ (metaphor) ایک چیز کو براہِ راست دوسری شے کی مانند بیان کرتا ہے تاکہ معنی گہرے ہوں۔

questions.q: پہیلی/محاورہ: 'اونٹ کے منہ میں کیا ڈالنا' عام مطلب؟
questions.ex: محاورہ 'اونٹ کے منہ میں کیا ڈالنا' کا مطلب ہے ایسی بیکار یا ناکافی کوشش جو فرق نہیں ڈالے گی۔

questions.q: درست فعل کی شکل منتخب کریں: 'وہ ہر روز کتابیں __۔'

questions.ex: یہ جملہ فصلوں کے فائدے بیان کرتا ہے، اس لیے 'توصیفی' صنف میں آتا ہے۔

questions.q: مکالماتی اصلاح: 'تم کیا کر رہے ہوں؟' کو درست کریں۔
questions.ex: مخاطب 'تم' کے ساتھ درست شکل 'تم کیا کر رہے ہو؟' ہے۔

questions.q: مناسب واحد/جمع کا انتخاب: 'ہر طالب علم __ گھر آیا.'

questions.q: قواعد: 'ہے' اور 'ہیں' میں فرق بتائیں — کون سی صورت خالصتاً جمع کے لیے؟
questions.ex: 'ہیں' عام طور پر جمع یا شائستہ 'آپ' کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے۔

questions.q: لفظی معنی: 'صحت' کا صحیح اردو معنی کیا ہے؟
questions.ex: 'صحت' کا مطلب 'تندرستی' ہے۔

questions.ex: عام املا 'چھتری' درست ہے۔

questions.q: مناسب درستگی: 'میں اسکول جاتا ہوں، وہ اسکول __.' (املا)

questions.q: اصل جملے کی شناخت: 'جس نے محنت کی وہ کامیاب ہوا' اس میں کون سا حرف ربط ہے؟
questions.ex: 'جس' ایک رشتہ دار حرفِ ربط/ضمیر ہے جو صیغہ ربط قائم کرتا ہے۔

questions.q: مناسب انتخاب: 'کھلونا' کا لفظ کس صنف کا ہے؟
questions.ex: 'کھلونا' ایک شے ہے، اس لیے اسم ہے۔

questions.q: ماضی اور حال میں فرق: 'میں کھاتا ہوں' اور 'میں کھایا' — کون سا جملہ ماضی ظاہر کرتا ہے؟
questions.ex: 'میں کھایا' ماضی کی طرف اشارہ کرتا ہے؛ 'میں کھاتا ہوں' حال بتاتا ہے۔

questions.q: درست سبق آموز جملہ: 'وقت کی پابندی ____.'
questions.ex: 'وقت کی پابندی اہم ہے۔' درست اور فصیح جملہ ہے۔

questions.q: صحیح جواب منتخب کریں: 'سب' کا مترادف کون سا؟

questions.q: کلاس روم سیناریو: اگر طالب علم 'میں نے کیا' کہتا ہے جب وہ 'میں نے کیا' کہنا چاہتا تھا، آپ استاد کیسے درست کریں؟
options: دیکھ کر درست کریں: 'میں نے کیا کیا'
questions.ex: غلطی لفظ ترتیب کی ہے؛ سادہ رہنمائی میں استاد 'میں نے کیا کہا' بتا کر درست تلفظ/ترتیب سکھائے گا۔

questions.q: یہ کون سا اسمِ مقام ہے: 'کتاب خانہ'؟
questions.ex: 'کتاب خانہ' مخصوص جگہ بتاتا ہے، اس لیے اسمِ مقام ہے۔

questions.q: کیا جملہ منطقی ہے؟ 'درخت نے پھل کھائے.'
questions.ex: یہ جملہ منطقی نہیں کیونکہ درخت خود پھل نہیں کھاتا؛ انسان یا جانور کھاتے ہیں۔

questions.q: درست لفظ کا انتخاب: 'دل' کے مترادف میں کون سا لفظ آتا ہے؟
questions.ex: 'قلب' فارسی/اردو میں 'دل' کا مترادف ہے۔

questions.q: کون سا سوال وضاحتی/توضیحی قسم کا ہے؟
questions.ex: 'کیوں؟' سوال وضاحت اور وجہ طلب کرتا ہے، اس لیے تشریحی نوعیت کا ہے۔

questions.q: مصدر شناخت کریں: 'پڑھنا' کس قسم کا لفظ ہے؟
questions.ex: 'پڑھنا' فعل کا مصدر ہے جو عمل کا نام ہے۔

questions.q: گرامر اور کلاس روم: اگر ایک طالب علم کہتا ہے 'ہم نے سبق پڑھی' تو آپ کس طرح درس میں درست کریں گے؟
options: بتائیں: 'ہم نے سبق پڑھے' اگر گروپ مرد ہے۔
فرض کریں: 'ہم نے سبق پڑھی' درست ہے۔
questions.ex: اگر گروپ میں مرد طالب علم ہیں تو 'ہم نے سبق پڑھے' درست جملہ ہے؛ استاد گروپ کی جنس کے مطابق صیغہ درست کرائے گا۔

questions.q: تشریح: 'محاورہ' اور 'استعارہ' میں بنیادی فرق بیان کریں۔
options: محاورہ ترکیبی بولا ہوتا ہے، استعارہ علامتی موازنہ ہے۔
محاورہ تشبیہ ہے، استعارہ حقیقی معنی ہوتا ہے۔
محاورہ صرف مزاح میں آتا ہے۔
questions.ex: محاورہ ایک روایتی ترکیب/بول چال ہوتی ہے جب کہ استعارہ ایک شے کو دوسری شے کی مانند بیان کر کے معنی میں گہرائی لاتا ہے۔

questions.q: متن فہم: ایک پیراگراف میں مضمون نگار بارہ بار 'ہمدردی' کی بات کرتا ہے — یہ بیانیہ انداز میں ہے، تو اس کا محور کون سا ہوگا؟
questions.ex: جب مضمون بار بار 'ہمدردی' پر مرکز ہوتا ہے تو اس کا مرکزی خیال یا محور 'ہمدردی' ہوتا ہے۔

questions.q: لفظی تجزیہ: 'کتابوں' میں 'وں' لاحقہ کی گرامری حیثیت کیا ہے؟
questions.ex: 'وں' عمومی طور پر مظاہر جمع (genitive/oblique plural) کے لیے لاحقہ ہوتا ہے، اس طرح جمع یا مضافِ الیہ شکل میں استعمال ہوتا ہے۔

questions.q: ادبی سوال: متن میں 'تشبیہ' پہچاننے کا طریقہ کیا ہے؟
options: صرف شعر میں تشبیہ ملتی ہے۔
questions.ex: تشبیہ عام طور پر 'جیسا/جیسے/کی طرح' کے الفاظ کے استعمال سے ظاہر ہوتی ہے؛ یہ نشانِ تشبیہ پہچاننے کا آسان طریقہ ہے۔

questions.q: کلاس روم سیناریو: اگر طالب علم لفظ 'محبت' کے مترادف تلاش کرے اور 'پیار' پیش کرے، کیسے آگے بڑھیں؟
options: سراہیں اور مزید مترادفات جیسے 'عشق'، 'محبت' کی سطح بتائیں۔
questions.ex: سکھانے کا درست طریقہ سراہنا اور مختلف درجوں/سیاق کے مطابق مترادفات بتانا ہے۔

questions.q: مکالماتی درستگی: 'میں اسکول جانے ہوں' — بہتر درست شکل کیا ہوگی؟
questions.ex: صحیح اور فصیح شکل 'میں اسکول جا رہا ہوں۔' ہے جو حالِ جاری بیان کرتی ہے۔

questions.q: تشریحی سوال: 'قالب' اور 'مواد' کے مابین فرق ادبی مطالعے میں کیا اہمیت رکھتا ہے؟
options: قالب فارمیٹ یا ساخت ہے؛ مواد وہ پیغام ہے جو منتقل ہوتا ہے۔
قالب صرف شاعری کے لیے ہے۔
questions.ex: ادب میں قالب (form) وہ ساخت ہوتی ہے جس میں کہانی یا نظم پیش کی جاتی ہے جبکہ مواد (content) وہ معنی اور پیغام ہے؛ دونوں کا فرق تجزیہ میں اہم ہے۔

questions.q: نحوی ادراک: جملہ 'اس نے کہا کہ وہ آئے گا' — اس میں کون سا کلمہ ربط استعمال ہوا؟
questions.ex: 'کہ' ربطی کلمہ ہے جو براہِ راست گفتگویی جملے کو مبدل کرتا ہے: 'اس نے کہا کہ ...'۔

questions.q: لغوی استعمال: 'تین' کا لفظ جمع/عدد کے لحاظ سے کس صنف میں آتا ہے؟
questions.ex: 'تین' ایک عددی شمار لفظ ہے، یعنی عدد کی حیثیت رکھتا ہے۔

questions.q: معنوی اختلاف: 'علاقہ' اور 'علاقہ دار' میں فرق کیا ہے؟
options: 'علاقہ' جگہ ہے؛ 'علاقہ دار' وہ جو علاقے کا باشندہ ہو۔
questions.ex: 'علاقہ' مقام یا جگہ ہے جبکہ 'علاقہ دار' اس جگہ کا باشندہ یا رکن کو ظاہر کرتا ہے۔

questions.q: درست املا کا چیلنج: 'استعارہ' کا صحیح اردو ہجے کیا ہے؟
questions.ex: صحیح املا 'استعارہ' ہے جس کا مطلب metaphor ہوتا ہے۔

questions.q: ادبی تاریخی علم (بنیادی): بچوں کی کلاس میں نظم پڑھاتے وقت آپ کس بات پر زور دیں گے؟
options: تلفظ، وزن اور معنی کی سادہ تفہیم
مصنف کی ذاتی زندگی تفصیل سے
questions.ex: بچوں کی کلاس میں نظم پڑھانے کے دوران تلفظ، شعری وزن اور سادہ معنوی تفہیم پر زور دینا مناسب ہے۔

questions.q: منطقی تجزیہ: 'اگر بارش ہوگی تو فصلیں اچھی ہوں گی' — یہ جملہ کس طرح کا منطقی ڈھانچہ ہے؟
questions.ex: یہ ایک شرطی جملہ ہے جو ایک نتیجہ کو ممکنہ شرط کے ساتھ جوڑتا ہے۔

questions.q: فعل کی جہت: 'کھانا' اور 'کھا رہا ہے' میں فرق کیا ہے؟
options: پہلا مصدر ہے، دوسرا حالِ استمرار بتاتا ہے۔
questions.ex: 'کھانا' مصدر ہے (infinitive) جبکہ 'کھا رہا ہے' جاری فعل کی حالت (present continuous) ظاہر کرتا ہے۔

questions.q: افہام و تفہیم: نص میں مضامین کو ترتیب دینے کا بہترین طریقہ کیا ہے؟
options: مرکزی خیال پہلے، تفصیلات بعد میں
تمام تفصیلات یکجا کر کے آخر میں مرکزی خیال
questions.ex: عام طور پر اچھے پیراگراف میں مرکزی خیال پہلے یا ابتدائی حصے میں ہوتا ہے، پھر اس کی تفصیلات آتی ہیں۔

questions.q: شعری شناخت: کون سا جملہ 'تشبیہ' ہے؟
options: اس کی آواز شیریں کی طرح ہے۔
questions.ex: 'اس کی آواز شیریں کی طرح ہے' واضح تشبیہ ہے کیونکہ 'کی طرح' کا استعمال ہوا ہے۔

questions.q: لغت و استعمال: 'مؤثر' اور 'بااثر' میں فرق بیان کریں۔
options: 'مؤثر' چیز کا اثر دکھاتا ہے؛ 'بااثر' شخص یا چیز کا اثر رکھنے والا۔
دونوں صرف رسمی زبان میں آتے ہیں۔
questions.ex: 'مؤثر' عام طور پر اثر ڈالنے والی خصوصیت بتاتا ہے، جبکہ 'بااثر' وہ جس کے پاس اثر یا طاقت ہو؛ معنا میں فرق استعمال کے مطابق ہوتا ہے۔

questions.q: پڑھائی کی حکمتِ عملی: نثر کی سمجھ بڑھانے کے لیے کون سی تکنیک کلاس میں مفید ہے؟
options: خلاصہ لکھوانا اور مرکزی نکات پر سوالات کرنا
مصنف کی ذاتی زندگی بیان کروانا
questions.ex: خلاصہ لکھوانا اور مرکزی نکات پر سوالات کرنا طلبہ کی فهم کو بہتر بناتا ہے۔

questions.q: نحو کا تجزیہ: 'میں نے اسے کتاب دی' میں 'سے' کس قسم کا لفظ ہے؟
questions.ex: 'اُسے' مفعولی ضمیر ہے جو مفعول کو ظاہر کرتا ہے؛ 'سے' یہاں موجود نہیں۔ تاہم جملے میں 'میں نے اُسے کتاب دی' میں 'اُسے' مفعولی ضمیر ہے۔

questions.q: مخالف صورتحال: 'سخت' کے معانی میں کون سا لفظ متضاد نہیں؟
questions.ex: 'تیز' 'سخت' کا متضاد نہیں بلکہ کسی اور وصف سے متعلق ہے؛ 'نرم'، 'نازک'، 'ملائم' متضاد یا قریب المعنی ہو سکتے ہیں۔

questions.q: تشخیص: جب بچے 'مترادف' الجھیں، آپ کون سا تکنیک استعمال کریں گے؟
options: لفظی کھیل اور مثالیں جو سیاق بدل کر دکھائیں
ان کو الفاظ یاد کروائیں بغیر معنی
محض پرکھ کے ذریعے سزا دیں
questions.ex: لفظی کھیل، سیاقی مثالیں اور تصویری معاونت مترادفات سکھانے میں مددگار ہوتے ہیں۔

questions.q: ترکیب و معنی: جملہ 'کتاب نے طالب کو سکھایا' میں کون سی لسانی غلطی ہے؟
options: انسانی فعل کو بےجان شے میں عائد کرنا (anthropomorphism) یا ساختی غلطی
questions.ex: جملے میں بےجان چیز 'کتاب' کو عامل بتا دیا گیا؛ حقیقی طور پر 'طالب' نے کتاب سے سیکھا، اس لیے ساختی طور پر 'طالب نے کتاب سے کچھ سیکھا' بہتر ہے۔

questions.q: ادبی مباحثہ: آپ ایک چھوٹی کلاس میں 'کہانی کا مرکزی خیال' کیسے چیک کریں گے؟
options: طلبہ سے ایک لائن میں مرکزی خیال لکھوائیں اور بحث کروائیں
مصنف کو طلبہ کے زور پر بلا کر تشریح کروائیں
questions.ex: مختصر اور مؤثر طریقہ یہ ہے کہ طلبہ سے ایک لائن میں مرکزی خیال لکھوایا جائے اور پھر مختصر بحث کے ذریعے جائزہ لیا جائے۔

questions.q: املا و قواعد: لفظ 'تقدیر' کا درست ہجے اور معنی کیا ہیں؟
questions.ex: 'تقدیر' عام طور پر 'قسمت' یا 'نصیب' کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے؛ یہی درست ہجے اور معنی ہیں۔

questions.q: پریکٹیکل کلاس روم: مضمون لکھنے میں طلبہ کو کون سی ہدایت سب سے پہلے دیں گے؟
options: مرکزی خیال کا انتخاب اور خاکہ بنانا
questions.ex: مضبوط مضمون کے لیے سب سے پہلے مرکزی خیال اور اس کا خاکہ بنانا ضروری ہے؛ یہ رہنمائی طلبہ کو منظم تحریر سکھاتی ہے۔

questions.q: زبانی اظہار: 'ہم نے مل کر کھانا کھایا' جملے میں 'مل کر' کا نحوی کردار کیا ہے؟
questions.ex: 'مل کر' حالت یا طریق بتاتا ہے یعنی حالتِ عمل (adverbial phrase) ہے؛ یہ بتاتا ہے کہ کام کس طرح ہوا۔

questions.q: تشریح: 'ضمیر اور صفت میں فرق' بتائیں۔
options: ضمیر نام بدلتا ہے جیسے 'وہ'؛ صفت اسم کی خصوصیت بتاتی ہے جیسے 'اچھا'۔
ضمیر صرف جمع میں آتا ہے۔
questions.ex: ضمیر اسم کی جگہ لیتا ہے (مثلاً 'وہ') جبکہ صفت اسم کی خصوصیات بتاتی ہے (مثلاً 'اچھا') — یہ بنیادی فرق ہے۔

questions.q: ادبی تجزیہ: جب ایک پیراگراف میں متضاد خیالیں ہوں، آپ طالب علم کو کیا سکھائیں گے؟
options: اہم نکات نمایاں کریں اور دونوں جانب کے دلائل کا موازنہ کرائیں
صرف ایک طرف کی حمایت کروائیں
متضاد خیالات کو نظر انداز کرو
questions.ex: طالب علم کو دونوں متضاد دلائل کا موازنہ سکھانا تنقیدی سوچ کو فروغ دیتا ہے؛ اہم نکات نمایاں کرنا مفید ہے۔

questions.q: لغوی تفہیم: 'نماز' ایک ______ ہے۔
questions.ex: 'نماز' ایک عبادت/عمل کا اسم ہے؛ اس لیے یہ اسم درجہ بندی ہے۔

questions.q: What is the primary focus of teacher-centred approaches?
options: Teacher as the main source of knowledge
questions.ex: Teacher-centred approaches emphasize the teacher delivering content and controlling instruction; the teacher is the primary knowledge source.

questions.q: Which Bloom's Taxonomy level involves remembering facts?
questions.ex: Remembering is the lowest level of Bloom's Taxonomy and refers to recall of facts and basic concepts.

questions.q: What does 'differentiated instruction' primarily address?
questions.ex: Differentiated instruction means varying content, process, or product to meet diverse learners' needs.

questions.q: Which strategy is an example of cooperative learning?
questions.ex: Think-Pair-Share involves students thinking individually, then discussing with a partner, a cooperative learning technique.

questions.q: Effective questioning that encourages higher-order thinking typically uses which type of question?
questions.ex: Open-ended questions prompt explanation, reasoning and higher-order thinking rather than simple recall.

questions.q: What is one key element of a lesson plan?
questions.ex: Learning objectives state what students should know or be able to do by the end of the lesson and are central to lesson planning.

questions.q: Active learning most often requires students to:
questions.ex: Active learning involves students actively participating in tasks, discussion, problem-solving or hands-on activities.

questions.q: Which of the following is a formative assessment?
questions.ex: A classroom exit ticket is a short, ongoing check for understanding used formatively to guide instruction.

questions.q: Which classroom activity best supports developing communication skills?
questions.ex: Pair role-play involves speaking and listening opportunities that build communication skills.

questions.q: National Professional Standards for Teachers (NPST) in Pakistan emphasize which of the following?
questions.ex: NPST emphasizes ongoing professional development to improve teacher effectiveness and student learning.

questions.q: A teacher uses a short quiz after a lesson to check understanding. This is called:
questions.ex: Short quizzes during instruction are formative assessments used to monitor learning and adjust teaching.

questions.q: Which questioning move helps students expand on their answers?
questions.ex: Asking for justification encourages students to explain and elaborate, deepening understanding.

questions.q: Which technique is student-centred?
questions.ex: Project-based learning centers students in constructing knowledge through inquiry and real tasks.

questions.q: In cooperative learning, 'positive interdependence' means:
options: Students work on identical tasks separately
Group members rely on each other to succeed
Teacher gives one member all answers
questions.ex: Positive interdependence requires group members to depend on each other's contributions to achieve the goal.

questions.q: An example of differentiated product might be:
options: Choice of poster, essay or oral presentation
questions.ex: Differentiated products offer varied ways for students to demonstrate learning suited to their strengths.

questions.q: Which is a characteristic of effective lesson objectives?
questions.ex: Effective objectives are specific and measurable so both teachers and students know expected outcomes.

questions.q: When implementing active learning, teachers should:
options: Lectures for whole period without activities
Provide tasks that require student engagement
questions.ex: Active learning requires tasks that engage students in thinking, discussion, or doing during lessons.

questions.q: Which Bloom's level requires breaking information into parts to explore relationships?
questions.ex: Analyzing involves examining components and relationships within information or concepts.

questions.q: A quick diagnostic at the start of a lesson to determine prior knowledge is called:
questions.ex: Pre-assessments or diagnostic checks identify students' prior knowledge before instruction.

questions.q: Which approach is best for maintaining classroom management during group work?
questions.ex: Clear roles and expectations help groups stay focused and productive during cooperative tasks.

questions.q: Scaffolding in teaching means:
options: Supporting students gradually until they are independent
questions.ex: Scaffolding provides support that is gradually removed as learners gain independence.

questions.q: Which learning activity promotes higher-order thinking per Bloom?
questions.ex: Designing an experiment involves creating, applying knowledge, and evaluating — higher-order thinking.

questions.q: An effective classroom question should ideally be:
questions.ex: Clear, purposeful questions target specific learning goals and guide student thinking.

questions.q: Which is a teacher-centred assessment practice?
questions.ex: Standardized or teacher-administered tests reflect teacher-centred assessment rather than student-led evaluation.

questions.q: Formative feedback should be:
questions.ex: Effective formative feedback is timely and specific to help students improve during learning.

questions.q: Which is an instructional approach that explicitly teaches skills step-by-step?
questions.ex: Direct instruction involves explicit, structured teaching of skills with modeling and practice.

questions.q: What does 'active listening' in classroom discussion involve?
options: Summarizing and responding to others' points
questions.ex: Active listening requires attending to, summarizing and building on others' contributions.

questions.q: In lesson planning, 'assessment criteria' are used to:
options: Clarify how work will be judged
questions.ex: Assessment criteria communicate expectations and how student work will be evaluated.

questions.q: Which strategy helps differentiated instruction for mixed-ability math class?
questions.ex: Tiered tasks allow students to work at different levels of difficulty while learning the same concept.

questions.q: A learning objective written as 'Students will be able to compare and contrast two stories' targets which cognitive skill?
questions.ex: Comparing and contrasting requires analyzing relationships and differences—analyzing level.

questions.q: A teacher notices three students struggling with a lesson while others progress. Best differentiated action is to:
options: Give the three students extra identical homework
Provide targeted small-group instruction on specific difficulties
Ignore and continue with full-class pace
Move them to a different class immediately
questions.ex: Targeted small-group instruction addresses specific gaps while keeping whole-class instruction moving.

questions.q: During a science lesson, teacher asks students to predict outcomes, test, then reflect. This sequence aligns with which instructional approach?
questions.ex: Inquiry-based learning uses prediction, experimentation and reflection to construct understanding.

questions.q: Which question would best assess application-level thinking (Bloom) in a math class?
options: Use addition to solve a word problem about shopping
questions.ex: Solving a real-world word problem requires applying addition skills in context, matching application level.

questions.q: A cooperative learning structure where individuals are accountable and teach each other is called:
questions.ex: Jigsaw assigns each student a piece to learn and teach peers, promoting interdependence and accountability.

questions.q: Which assessment practice aligns with NPST's emphasis on improving instruction?
options: Using assessment data to inform future teaching
questions.ex: NPST promotes using assessment data formatively to guide planning and professional growth.

questions.q: A lesson plan includes 'students will summarize main ideas after reading.' What is an appropriate assessment task?
options: Ask students to write a one-paragraph summary
Ask students to memorize the paragraph verbatim
questions.ex: Writing a summary directly assesses the stated learning objective of summarizing main ideas.

questions.q: Which strategy promotes active learning in a history lesson for Class 6?
options: Teacher reads textbook for full period
Students act out historical events in role-play
questions.ex: Role-play engages students actively in understanding historical perspectives and events.

questions.q: A teacher uses wait-time after asking a complex question. Expected effect is:
questions.ex: Longer wait-time allows students to think and formulate deeper, higher-quality responses.

questions.q: Which formative assessment is most useful for adapting next lesson's instruction?
options: Exit ticket indicating two things learned and one question
Final project graded after course end
questions.ex: Exit tickets give quick insight into student understanding and immediate instructional needs.

questions.q: How can a teacher support differentiated instruction for English language learners?
options: Provide visuals and simplified language supports
questions.ex: Visuals and language supports scaffold comprehension and participation for ELL students.

questions.q: An effective cooperative learning assessment includes:
options: Only group grade applied to everyone
Random grading by teacher without criteria
questions.ex: Combining individual accountability with group assessment ensures fair evaluation of contributions and outcomes.

questions.q: Which questioning move encourages students to connect ideas across subjects?
options: Ask questions limited to one fact
Prompt for real-world connections and transfer
questions.ex: Prompts that ask students to relate concepts to other subjects encourage transfer and deeper understanding.

questions.q: A teacher plans a lesson to reach 'understanding' level of Bloom. Which activity fits best?
options: Paraphrasing concept in own words with examples
Only filling blanks in a worksheet
questions.ex: Paraphrasing with examples shows comprehension beyond mere memorization—understanding level.

questions.q: During peer assessment, a teacher should ensure students:
questions.ex: Clear rubrics and guidance help peers provide constructive, aligned feedback during peer assessment.

questions.q: Which lesson planning element helps differentiate pacing for learners?
options: Time allocations with flexible extension activities
questions.ex: Including flexible timing and extension/extra practice options allows teachers to adjust pacing.

questions.q: In a mixed-ability science class, a tiered assignment achieves differentiation by:
options: Providing tasks at varying levels of complexity toward same goal
Lowering standards for some students only
questions.ex: Tiered assignments ensure all students work on essential concepts but at different challenge levels.

questions.q: Which active-learning technique is suitable for developing critical thinking in Class 7 social studies?
options: Students create and defend a mock council decision
questions.ex: Creating and defending decisions requires analysis, argumentation and evaluation—fostering critical thinking.

questions.q: A teacher-centred approach is most appropriate when:
options: Students must discover complex principles unaided
Introducing foundational skills requiring direct modeling
questions.ex: Direct modelling and guided practice are effective when teaching foundational skills that need explicit instruction.

questions.q: Which is an example of integrating Bloom's 'creating' in a language lesson?
options: Students invent an original short story based on theme
questions.ex: Creating original work applies knowledge creatively, matching the highest level of Bloom's taxonomy.

questions.q: What is the role of 'learning objectives' in formative assessment?
options: To guide what is assessed and feedback provided
questions.ex: Learning objectives define targets for assessment and shape the feedback provided to students.

questions.q: Which approach helps manage noisy group work while keeping students engaged?
options: Provide clear task instructions and noise-level expectations
questions.ex: Clear instructions and expectations allow active group work while maintaining acceptable behaviour.

questions.q: A teacher wants students to evaluate multiple solutions to a problem. Which Bloom level is targeted?
questions.ex: Evaluating involves judging the merits of ideas, solutions or methods, matching that Bloom level.

questions.q: Which lesson closure technique helps consolidate learning?
options: Summarizing key points and asking students to reflect
questions.ex: Summarizing and reflection help students consolidate learning and connect lesson elements.

questions.q: How can technology support differentiated instruction in Class 5?
options: By forcing same pacing for all
By offering adaptive learning programs and choice of resources
By only playing videos with no interaction
questions.ex: Adaptive programs and varied resources allow students to work at appropriate levels and styles.

questions.q: Which practice aligns with NPST competency for inclusive classroom?
options: Excluding students with learning difficulties from activities
Adapting instruction for diverse learner needs
questions.ex: NPST emphasizes inclusive practices—adapting teaching to meet diverse learner needs in the classroom.

questions.q: When designing assessments, validity refers to:
options: Whether it measures what it intends to measure
How fast it can be graded
questions.ex: Validity concerns whether assessment tasks accurately measure the intended learning objectives.

questions.q: Which questioning format best checks students' procedural fluency in mathematics?
options: Ask for steps to solve a problem, not just the answer
Ask only conceptual history of maths
Only ask students to re-state the question
questions.ex: Requesting procedural steps reveals students' fluency and understanding of the method, beyond the final answer.

questions.q: A teacher using project-based learning should ensure projects are:
options: Aligned with clear objectives and assessment criteria
questions.ex: Effective project-based learning aligns projects with objectives and criteria so learning is purposeful and assessable.

questions.q: Which classroom arrangement best supports cooperative learning for group tasks?
options: Rows facing front with no grouping
Teacher desk centered and students isolated
questions.ex: Clusters allow communication and collaboration needed for cooperative learning activities.

questions.q: A teacher observes that many students copy answers during group work. Best assessment adjustment is to:
options: Include individual accountability components like reflections or quizzes
Give the same grade to everyone regardless
questions.ex: Including individual assessments ensures each student's understanding is evaluated and discourages copying.

questions.q: A Class 7 science teacher plans an inquiry activity. Some students lack background knowledge required. How should the teacher sequence learning?
options: Provide targeted mini-lessons (scaffolds) on prerequisite concepts, then proceed with inquiry
Give students the final conclusion to memorize
questions.ex: Scaffolding prerequisite knowledge before inquiry enables meaningful investigation while maintaining inquiry's benefits.

questions.q: During a lesson, a teacher notices divergent answers from students. To use this productively, the teacher should:
options: Correct all but the majority view
Facilitate a discussion comparing reasoning and evidence behind different answers
Ignore minority answers and move on
questions.ex: Discussing varied answers helps students confront reasoning, develop critical thinking and refine understanding.

questions.q: A math teacher wants to assess higher-order thinking. Which assessment design is best?
options: Open-ended problems requiring strategy explanation and justification
questions.ex: Open-ended problems that require strategies and justification assess analysis, synthesis and evaluation.

questions.q: A teacher-centred lecture covered content but students failed to transfer learning to new contexts. Which change would likely improve transfer?
options: Incorporate active learning tasks requiring application and varied practice
questions.ex: Active tasks and varied contexts during instruction promote deeper understanding and ability to transfer learning.

questions.q: A teacher uses heterogeneous groups but notices dominant students lead all tasks. To promote equitable participation, the teacher should:
options: Assign rotating roles and teach collaborative skills
Assign all leadership tasks to dominant students
Keep groups the same without intervention
questions.ex: Structured roles and explicit collaborative skill instruction help balance participation and develop all students' abilities.

questions.q: How can Bloom's Taxonomy guide writing assessment rubrics in a Class 6 language unit?
options: Ignore taxonomy and use only length-based grading
Create rubric criteria that target comprehension, application, analysis and creation levels
Use only spelling and punctuation as criteria
Rely solely on teacher impression without descriptors
questions.ex: Rubrics aligned with Bloom help assess different cognitive levels, providing clear expectations for depth of thinking.

questions.q: A teacher wants to design a formative assessment to inform immediate reteaching. Which feature is most critical?
options: Rapid, specific feedback loop and actionable data
Long scoring process with complex analytics
questions.ex: Formative assessments must provide quick, actionable feedback so the teacher can adjust instruction promptly.

questions.q: During lesson planning, aligning objectives, activities and assessments is called:
questions.ex: Backward design starts with desired outcomes and aligns activities and assessments to those objectives.

questions.q: A teacher uses peer tutoring where stronger students help weaker ones. To ensure cognitive challenge for both, teacher should:
options: Have tutors only copy answers for tutees
Provide tutors with teaching prompts and tutees with reflective tasks
Let tutors do the work for tutees
questions.ex: Providing prompts and reflective tasks engages tutors in explaining (which deepens their understanding) and prompts tutees to process learning.

questions.q: Which questioning sequence best moves students from understanding to evaluation?
options: Ask them to recall facts, then apply in a scenario, then critique possible solutions
Ask only one complex question at the end
questions.ex: Progressing from recall to application to critique scaffolds cognitive development toward evaluation-level thinking.

questions.q: A Class 5 teacher must assess students with varied literacy levels. Which assessment approach supports fairness and validity?
options: Offer multimodal assessments (oral explanations, drawings, practical tasks) aligned to objectives
Grade solely on effort without evidence of learning
questions.ex: Multimodal assessments allow students to demonstrate learning in different modes, improving fairness and validity.

questions.q: To promote metacognition in students, a teacher can:
options: Ask students to reflect on strategies used and what they would change
questions.ex: Reflection on strategies encourages awareness of thinking and helps students plan and regulate learning.

questions.q: An instructional sequence for a new grammar concept should include which order for effective learning?
options: Assessment, immediate summative test, no instruction
Introduce concept with modeling, guided practice, independent practice, assessment
questions.ex: Effective sequence begins with explicit instruction and modeling, then guided practice, independent practice and assessment.

questions.q: A teacher evaluates lesson effectiveness by student work and finds misconceptions. Best next step is to:
options: Design a targeted reteach using formative techniques and misconceptions as teaching points
Lower standards to hide the problem
Give more homework without addressing misconceptions
questions.ex: Using student work to inform targeted reteaching addresses misconceptions and improves subsequent learning.

questions.q: Which strategy best supports inclusion of students with learning disabilities in cooperative tasks?
options: Assign them isolated simpler tasks away from peers
Provide role adaptations, explicit directions and peer support within group tasks
Expect them to perform at same pace without supports
questions.ex: Adapting roles and providing scaffolds enables participation and learning within inclusive cooperative activities.

questions.q: A teacher-centred direct instruction lesson shows high accuracy on practiced tasks but poor transfer. Which modification supports deeper learning?
options: Add varied contexts and problem-solving opportunities after initial skill mastery
Increase repetition of same tasks indefinitely
questions.ex: After mastering routine skill, varied practice and problem-solving promote transfer to novel situations.

questions.q: When designing a summative assessment aligned to a unit, the most important validation step is to:
options: Ensure it covers only rare trivia
Map items to stated objectives and ensure content coverage and cognitive demand match
Make it extremely long regardless of content
Include unrelated topics to increase difficulty
questions.ex: Valid summative assessments sample content and cognitive levels specified in objectives to accurately measure outcomes.

questions.q: In a classroom discussion, some students dominate while others stay silent. A teacher-centred corrective move would be:
options: Call on quieter students with thought-time and use protocols like 'think-pair-share'
questions.ex: Structured participation strategies encourage balanced contributions while still teacher-guided.

questions.q: A unit uses project-based learning but students produce low-quality projects and miss standards. Why likely, and what remedy?
options: Projects are always inferior; stop using them
Probably lack of clear criteria and supports; provide rubrics, milestones, modelling and formative checkpoints
Give grades based on effort only
Let students choose any unrelated topic without guidance
questions.ex: Clear criteria, scaffolds and formative feedback are necessary to guide students toward meeting standards in project work.

questions.q: A teacher wants to measure growth in critical thinking over a term. Best instrument type is:
options: Single multiple-choice test at start only
Performance tasks with rubrics administered at multiple points
questions.ex: Performance tasks with rubrics given across time capture development in critical thinking more effectively than single tests.

questions.q: A lesson plan includes activities, but assessment is unrelated. This misalignment causes:
options: Confusion about expectations and unreliable measurement of objectives
questions.ex: When assessments don't align with objectives and activities, they fail to validly measure intended learning and confuse students.

questions.q: Which differentiation strategy is most sustainable for a busy primary teacher?
options: Prepare entirely separate lessons for each student
Use flexible grouping and tiered tasks that reuse core planning with varying supports
Avoid planning and improvise every day
questions.ex: Flexible grouping and tiered tasks allow differentiation with manageable planning by reusing core materials but varying demands.

questions.q: A teacher wants to foster higher-order questions among students. Best classroom routine to develop this is:
options: Model question stems, practice generating questions and use them in peer discussions
Expect students to generate high-level questions without scaffolding
questions.ex: Teaching question stems and practicing question generation builds students' capacity to ask deeper, higher-order questions.

questions.q: When analyzing assessment data, a teacher finds a specific misconception across classes. Most effective school-level response is:
options: Organize collaborative professional learning to design common interventions and resources
questions.ex: Collaborative professional learning enables teachers to design targeted interventions and share strategies to address common misconceptions.

questions.q: Which strategy best differentiates instruction for gifted students within a Class 6 mixed classroom?
options: Require them to tutor others exclusively
Provide compacting, enrichment, and open-ended extension tasks aligned to the same objectives
Give them no work to avoid boredom
questions.ex: Curriculum compacting and enrichment allow gifted students to progress and deepen learning while aligned to objectives.

questions.q: A teacher uses questioning to check comprehension but notices superficial answers. Which follow-up move deepens responses?
options: Ask probing follow-up prompts such as 'Why do you think that?' and 'Can you provide evidence?'
Accept the first quick answer and move on
Only call on same confident students
questions.ex: Probing follow-ups push students to justify and elaborate, improving depth of responses.

questions.q: A formative assessment shows two clusters of learners: one mastered objectives, one not. Best next-step planning is to:
options: Teach the same lesson to entire class again at same pace
Use flexible grouping: enrichment for mastery group and focused reteach for others with targeted supports
Ignore differences and give punishing homework
questions.ex: Flexible grouping provides appropriate challenge for mastery learners while giving targeted instruction to those who need support.

questions.q: Which element is essential when creating a rubric for a Class 4 science project?
options: Specific criteria with performance levels and clear descriptors tied to objectives
questions.ex: Rubrics need clear criteria and descriptions of performance levels so students understand expectations and assessment is reliable.

questions.q: A teacher aims to improve student-centred learning but parents expect teacher-led instruction. Best approach is to:
options: Comply only with parents and maintain lecture style
Communicate rationale, show evidence of student-centred benefits and invite parents to observed lessons
questions.ex: Engaging parents with rationale, evidence and opportunities to observe helps build understanding and support for student-centred approaches.

questions.q: Which instructional move fosters transfer when teaching reading comprehension strategies?
options: Teach strategies across multiple texts and disciplines with explicit prompts to apply them
Teach strategy once on a single passage only
Avoid teaching strategies; expect students to infer them
Use strategy only in isolation without connection to content
questions.ex: Repeated practice across texts and disciplines with explicit transfer prompts helps students apply strategies in new contexts.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the primary aim of basic education in Pakistan for grades 1-8?
options: Developing literacy, numeracy and basic life skills
Training students exclusively for religious studies
Focusing only on rote memorization of facts
questions.ex: Basic education (grades 1-8) emphasizes literacy, numeracy and foundational life skills rather than immediate job training or only rote learning.

questions.q: Who is known as the father of modern education and promoted learning through discovery and experience?
questions.ex: John Dewey advocated progressive education and learning through experience and reflection.

questions.q: Which level of Bloom's taxonomy involves remembering facts?
questions.ex: Remembering is the lowest level in Bloom's taxonomy, involving recall of facts and basic concepts.

questions.q: Which branch of foundations of education studies how society and culture influence education?
questions.ex: Sociological foundations examine the relationship between society, culture and educational processes.

questions.q: What is formative assessment primarily used for?
options: Monitoring student learning to inform instruction
questions.ex: Formative assessment is used to monitor learning and provide feedback to improve teaching and learning.

questions.q: In the context of classroom teaching, which method best supports active learning for young learners?
questions.ex: Interactive group activities engage young learners and support active learning and social skills.

questions.q: Which psychological theory emphasizes stages of cognitive development in children?
questions.ex: Jean Piaget proposed stage-based cognitive development (sensorimotor, preoperational, concrete operational, formal operational).

questions.q: Which document outlines the national education policy and objectives in Pakistan?
questions.ex: The National Education Policy sets national-level objectives and guidance for Pakistan's education system.

questions.q: What is a key characteristic of a learner-centered classroom?
options: Instruction tailored to students' needs and interests
questions.ex: Learner-centered classrooms adapt instruction to students' needs, interests and prior knowledge.

questions.q: Which term refers to rules, norms and practices transmitted through schooling and social institutions?
questions.ex: Hidden curriculum consists of implicit values, norms and expectations conveyed in school culture and practices.

questions.q: Who stresses the importance of social interaction for cognitive development (zone of proximal development)?
questions.ex: Vygotsky introduced the zone of proximal development and emphasized social interaction in learning.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of inclusive education practice?
questions.ex: Inclusive education adapts instruction and environment to meet diverse learners' needs within mainstream classrooms.

questions.q: What does 'curriculum' commonly refer to in basic schooling?
questions.ex: Curriculum encompasses planned learning experiences, objectives, content, methods and assessments.

questions.q: Which philosopher believed that education should cultivate rational individuals and citizens?
questions.ex: Plato emphasized education for cultivating reason and preparing individuals for civic life.

questions.q: Which assessment practice is most appropriate for evaluating a student's reading progress in grade 3?
options: Regular running records and observational notes
questions.ex: Running records and teacher observations provide ongoing information on a grade 3 student's reading development.

questions.q: What is the main role of the teacher in a constructivist classroom?
questions.ex: In constructivism, teachers facilitate learners' active construction of knowledge through tasks and guidance.

questions.q: Which historical foundation helps teachers understand the evolution of education systems?
questions.ex: Historical foundations examine past practices and reforms, giving context to current education systems.

questions.q: Which of the following is an objective of primary education under Pakistan's curriculum?
options: Development of basic literacy and numeracy
Training in specialized vocational trades only
questions.ex: Primary education aims to develop basic literacy, numeracy and foundational skills for further learning.

questions.q: Which sociological concept refers to transmission of cultural values through schools?
questions.ex: Socialization is the process through which schools transmit cultural values, norms and behaviors to students.

questions.q: Which classroom practice supports moral development in young children?
options: Discussing ethical dilemmas and modeling behavior
questions.ex: Discussing moral dilemmas and modeling respectful behavior help children's moral development.

questions.q: What is the main focus of educational psychology for teachers?
options: Understanding how students learn and develop
questions.ex: Educational psychology helps teachers understand learning processes, development and instructional strategies.

questions.q: Which principle should guide lesson planning for mixed-ability grade 4 classes?
options: One single task for all students
questions.ex: Differentiation provides varied supports and tasks to match students' diverse readiness and needs.

questions.q: Which of the following is a characteristic of a democratic school environment?
options: Encouragement of participation and respect for rights
questions.ex: Democratic schools encourage student participation, shared decision-making and respect for rights.

questions.q: Which teaching approach uses small, mixed-ability groups to promote learning?
questions.ex: Cooperative learning organizes students into groups where they work together and support each other's learning.

questions.q: Which factor is most important when selecting culturally relevant materials for class 1-5?
options: Relevance to students' local culture and experiences
questions.ex: Culturally relevant materials connect learning to students' lives and improve engagement and comprehension.

questions.q: Which legal document in Pakistan guarantees the right to education?
questions.ex: The Constitution of Pakistan includes provisions that support the right to education and state responsibilities.

questions.q: Which assessment is most useful for planning the next lesson in grade 2 math?
questions.ex: Diagnostic/pre-assessment identifies students' current understanding and informs lesson planning.

questions.q: Which teacher quality most influences student achievement in early grades?
options: Content knowledge and pedagogy for young learners
questions.ex: Teachers' content knowledge and pedagogical skills are strong predictors of student learning, especially in early grades.

questions.q: What is the hidden curriculum often observed in schools?
options: Implicit lessons about social roles and expectations
questions.ex: Hidden curriculum refers to implicit lessons students learn about norms, values and social expectations from school culture.

questions.q: Which early childhood principle supports hands-on sensory learning for grade 1?
questions.ex: Play-based, hands-on activities support young children's sensory, motor and cognitive development.

questions.q: A grade 4 teacher finds several students struggling with subtraction with regrouping. Which immediate instructional strategy is best?
options: Use manipulatives and concrete models to reteach the concept
Ignore and proceed with the next unit
questions.ex: Manipulatives help students visualize regrouping and build conceptual understanding before abstract practice.

questions.q: Which classroom assessment aligns best with learning outcomes emphasizing critical thinking in grade 6?
options: Performance task requiring explanation and reasoning
Only matching items on a worksheet
questions.ex: Performance tasks that require explanation and reasoning assess higher-order thinking aligned to critical thinking outcomes.

questions.q: A teacher notices that girls in a rural Sindh classroom rarely participate. Which action supports gender-equitable participation?
options: Use structured turn-taking and small-group tasks to encourage all voices
questions.ex: Structured strategies like turn-taking and small-group work create safe opportunities for girls to participate.

questions.q: How can a teacher integrate local culture into a grade 3 social studies lesson?
options: Include local stories, traditions and community resources
questions.ex: Incorporating local stories and community resources makes learning relevant and respects students' cultural backgrounds.

questions.q: Which method best assesses oral language development in class 2 Urdu?
questions.ex: Oral storytelling and observations allow teachers to evaluate fluency, vocabulary and expressive language skills.

questions.q: How should a teacher apply Vygotsky's concept of scaffolding while teaching new reading skills?
options: Provide step-by-step support and gradually withdraw it
Let students figure everything out alone
questions.ex: Scaffolding involves supporting learners initially and gradually reducing support as competence increases.

questions.q: Which classroom rule best supports inclusion for students with special needs?
options: Adapt tasks and provide peer support
Use standard worksheets for all without modification
questions.ex: Adapting tasks and using peer support enables participation and learning for students with special needs.

questions.q: In teaching science to grade 5, which approach reflects inquiry-based learning?
options: Designing simple experiments and drawing conclusions
questions.ex: Inquiry-based learning engages students in asking questions, experimenting and constructing explanations.

questions.q: Which assessment practice reduces cultural bias for multilingual students in grades 1-5?
options: Testing only in a language students don't know well
Allowing demonstrations, visual tasks and multiple modes of response
Using idiomatic language in all questions
questions.ex: Allowing varied response modes and culturally appropriate materials reduces bias and better captures learning.

questions.q: A teacher wants to foster civic values in grade 6. Which classroom activity is most effective?
options: Classroom community projects and discussions on responsibilities
questions.ex: Community projects and guided discussions help students practice civic responsibilities and understand their role.

questions.q: Which classroom seating arrangement best promotes peer collaboration in grade 4?
questions.ex: Clusters facilitate interaction and collaboration for group tasks and cooperative learning activities.

questions.q: How can teachers use formative assessment data to support low-achieving grade 3 students?
options: Differentiate instruction, provide targeted interventions and monitor progress
questions.ex: Formative data should guide differentiated instruction and targeted interventions to support progress.

questions.q: Which philosophy of education emphasizes self-actualization and students' potential?
questions.ex: Humanism focuses on individual growth, self-actualization and personal potential in education.

questions.q: A teacher observes disruptive behavior linked to unmet basic needs. What is an appropriate first step?
options: Identify and address the underlying needs (hunger, safety) before discipline
questions.ex: Addressing unmet basic needs is essential before applying disciplinary measures; behavior often improves when needs are met.

questions.q: Which policy action would most improve attendance in primary schools in rural Sindh?
options: Provide school meals and safe access to school
questions.ex: School meals and safe access (transport, safe routes) remove barriers to attendance in rural areas.

questions.q: How should a teacher integrate assessment for learning into daily instruction?
options: Use quick checks, exit tickets and feedback during lessons
questions.ex: Assessment for learning includes frequent, low-stakes checks and actionable feedback to inform teaching.

questions.q: Which technique helps develop mathematical reasoning in grade 5?
options: Presenting open-ended problems and encouraging multiple solution methods
questions.ex: Open-ended problems promote reasoning, flexibility and conceptual understanding in mathematics.

questions.q: What is the teacher's role in addressing cultural diversity in the classroom?
options: Respect, include and use diverse cultural resources in teaching
questions.ex: Teachers should respect and include diverse cultures, using them as assets for learning.

questions.q: Which historical factor shaped Pakistan's education system after 1947?
options: Complete continuity with pre-1947 systems without change
Partition and the need to develop a national education system
Adoption of a foreign language only
Uniform global education model without local adaptation
questions.ex: Partition required building new national institutions and policies, influencing the development of Pakistan's education system.

questions.q: How can teachers implement child protection measures in school?
options: Establish clear reporting procedures, trained staff and safe school policies
questions.ex: Child protection requires clear reporting, trained personnel and school policies to ensure safety and response.

questions.q: Which is an example of culturally responsive pedagogy in a language lesson?
options: Including students' home languages and familiar contexts in tasks
questions.ex: Culturally responsive pedagogy values students' home languages and contexts to make learning accessible.

questions.q: Which motivational strategy is effective for grade 2 learners?
options: Praise for effort, specific feedback and achievable goals
questions.ex: Specific praise for effort and clear, achievable goals foster intrinsic motivation in young learners.

questions.q: A school wants to improve teacher professional development in rural Sindh. Which approach is most sustainable?
options: Ongoing mentoring, in-class coaching and peer learning communities
questions.ex: Sustainable PD includes ongoing mentoring, coaching and collaborative learning rather than one-off workshops.

questions.q: Which ethical principle should guide classroom assessment?
questions.ex: Ethical assessment practices require fairness, transparency, validity and reliability in evaluating students.

questions.q: How can teachers use local community resources to enhance learning in grade 6 social studies?
options: Invite local elders, use field visits and community artifacts in lessons
questions.ex: Engaging local elders, visits and artifacts connects curriculum to students' lived experiences and enriches learning.

questions.q: Which approach best supports bilingual learners in early grades?
options: Translanguaging strategies and scaffolds in both languages
Waiting until high school to address language needs
questions.ex: Translanguaging allows strategic use of both languages to support comprehension and gradual development.

questions.q: Which historical concept helps teachers understand current inequities in education?
options: Studying past policies, colonial legacies and resource distribution
questions.ex: Historical study of past policies and legacies sheds light on structural causes of present inequities.

questions.q: How should a teacher adapt instruction for a student with hearing impairment in grade 4?
options: Use visual aids, captioned videos and preferential seating near the teacher
questions.ex: Visual supports, captioning and close seating improve access for students with hearing impairments.

questions.q: Which classroom practice most effectively develops scientific literacy in grade 7?
options: Engaging students in inquiry, evidence-based argumentation and real-world problems
questions.ex: Scientific literacy grows through inquiry, evidence evaluation and applying concepts to real-world contexts.

questions.q: How can teachers assess collaborative skills in group projects?
options: Use peer assessment, observation checklists and individual reflections
Assign same grade to all without assessment
questions.ex: Assessing collaboration uses multiple measures such as peer feedback, observations and reflections to capture teamwork skills.

questions.q: A grade 5 class includes students from two linguistic backgrounds. You must design a unit on local history. Which plan best balances content mastery and language development?
options: Teach exclusively in the dominant language and ignore the minority language
Use bilingual texts, partner reading across languages and tasks allowing expression in either language
Translate everything into the minority language only
Avoid language supports and focus on rote memorization
questions.ex: Bilingual texts and partner strategies support content learning while developing both languages and honoring students' identities.

questions.q: As headteacher you must address low student achievement school-wide. Which evidence-based policy is most effective long-term?
options: Increase class sizes to save costs
Invest in regular instructional coaching, curriculum alignment and data-informed interventions
questions.ex: Instructional coaching, aligned curriculum and data-driven interventions are proven to improve teaching and learning sustainably.

questions.q: A teacher observes persistent gender stereotyping in classroom materials. What is the best multi-step response?
options: Audit materials, select alternatives, involve students in critical discussions and train staff on gender sensitivity
questions.ex: Auditing materials, offering alternatives, facilitating critical discussions and staff training addresses stereotyping structurally and pedagogically.

questions.q: You are designing assessment for a grade 6 project on local ecosystems. Which combination provides valid, reliable and educationally useful data?
options: Rubric-based performance assessment, student reflections, and checklist of inquiry skills
Relying on peer popularity to grade work
questions.ex: Combining rubrics, reflections and skill checklists yields valid, transparent and useful information on both product and process.

questions.q: A parent-teacher conflict arises over corporal punishment. As a teacher, what is the appropriate course of action?
options: Explain school policy prohibiting corporal punishment, document concerns, follow child protection procedures and engage parents in positive discipline strategies
Use corporal punishment to assert authority
questions.ex: Teachers must adhere to child protection policies, document issues and work with parents on non-harmful discipline methods.

questions.q: In a diverse Grade 4 class, formative data show a wide spread in reading levels. How should the teacher allocate limited instructional time most effectively?
options: Use guided reading groups at levels, brief whole-class instruction and targeted interventions for struggling readers
Spend entire time on advanced readers
questions.ex: Guided reading groups, short whole-class lessons and targeted interventions maximize differentiation within limited time.

questions.q: A curriculum revision committee must ensure cultural relevance without compromising standards. Which approach balances both?
options: Replace all national standards with local content
Map learning outcomes to local contexts, include community knowledge as examples and retain core competencies
Lower standards to accommodate local content only
questions.ex: Mapping standards to local contexts and including community knowledge maintains competencies while making learning relevant.

questions.q: During a classroom observation, you notice a teacher uses predominantly didactic lectures with grade 3. How would you give constructive feedback to improve student engagement?
options: Tell them they are bad at teaching
Provide specific evidence from observation, suggest active strategies (think-pair-share, manipulatives), model one lesson and offer peer coaching
questions.ex: Constructive feedback includes evidence, practical alternatives, modeling and ongoing support like peer coaching.

questions.q: A research study shows socioeconomic status strongly predicts test scores in your district. As an education planner, which intervention mix tackles this inequity effectively?
options: Invest in early childhood programs, remedial coaching, school meals and community outreach to reduce barriers
Adopt a single top-down curriculum without supports
questions.ex: Combining early childhood investment, remedial help, nutrition and outreach addresses multiple barriers linked to socioeconomic inequality.

questions.q: You must design a professional development session on assessment literacy for grade 1-5 teachers. Which components are essential?
options: Practical rubric development, item writing, moderation exercises, scoring reliability practice and classroom application strategies
questions.ex: Effective PD includes hands-on work with rubrics, item writing, moderation and classroom application to build assessment literacy.

questions.q: In planning inclusive classrooms, how do you prioritize accommodations for limited resources while maximizing participation?
options: Provide full individual aids to one student only
Implement universal design for learning (multiple representations, simple adaptations) and train teachers in low-cost accommodations
Wait for outside funding before making any changes
questions.ex: Universal Design for Learning and low-cost adaptations enable broad accessibility without heavy resource demands.

questions.q: A historical study shows colonial-era policies shaped current rural school distribution. How should this insight inform current policy decisions?
options: Target resources to historically underserved areas and design context-sensitive reforms
questions.ex: Understanding historical inequities supports targeted resource allocation and context-aware reforms to redress past imbalances.

questions.q: A grade 7 science lesson on forces uses terminology unfamiliar to students. How should the teacher sequence instruction to build conceptual understanding?
options: Start with formal definitions and equations
Begin with concrete demonstrations, elicit prior ideas, use guided experiments, then formalize with vocabulary and symbols
Give a long lecture then a test
questions.ex: Concrete experiences and eliciting prior conceptions before formalization helps students build accurate scientific understanding.

questions.q: You observe frequent exam leakages in primary-level assessments. Which systemic changes reduce leak risk while maintaining assessment validity?
options: Use multiple assessment forms, in-school continuous assessment portfolios, secure item banks and randomization of papers
Allow open-book exams only for rote tasks
questions.ex: Combining secure item banks, varied assessment modes and continuous portfolios reduces leakage risk and preserves validity.

questions.q: A teacher must reconcile students' home cultural practices with national curriculum content that seems contradictory. What pedagogical stance is best?
options: Encourage critical reflection, compare perspectives, and allow students to relate curriculum to local practices respectfully
Punish students for adhering to home practices
Remove all local content from teaching
questions.ex: Encouraging respectful comparison and critical reflection helps students bridge local knowledge and national curriculum content.

questions.q: In a mixed-ability class, a teacher uses peer tutoring. Which structure maximizes learning for both tutor and tutee?
options: Train tutors in specific strategies, provide structured tasks and monitor interactions with brief feedback
Only have high-achievers do the work for low-achievers
questions.ex: Training, structured tasks and teacher monitoring ensure peer tutoring benefits both participants and keeps interactions instructional.

questions.q: Educational psychologists recommend early screening for learning difficulties. What is an appropriate school-level implementation for grades 1-3?
options: Brief validated screening tools, referral pathways, teacher training and classroom interventions for identified students
questions.ex: Brief screenings with clear referral and intervention pathways plus teacher training allow early support without stigma.

questions.q: A teacher must design a summative assessment for grade 4 science that aligns with inquiry objectives. Which item mix best matches the objective?
options: Practical task (short experiment write-up), short constructed responses for reasoning and a few MCQs for concepts
questions.ex: A mix of practical tasks, constructed responses and MCQs assesses inquiry skills, reasoning and factual understanding appropriately.

questions.q: A school implements a new child-centered pedagogy but sees teacher resistance. Which change-management approach is most likely to succeed?
options: Involve teachers in planning, provide training, model lessons, offer mentoring and allow phased implementation
questions.ex: Inclusive change management that engages teachers, provides support and phases in reforms fosters ownership and sustainable adoption.

questions.q: In designing a civic education lesson promoting tolerance, which assessment task best evaluates students' applied understanding?
options: A multiple-choice quiz on vocabulary only
Role-play and reflective journal where students respond to scenarios requiring tolerant actions
questions.ex: Role-play plus reflection assesses students' ability to apply tolerant behaviors in realistic situations.

questions.q: How can teachers use local religious festivals to teach about social cohesion without promoting one religion over others?
options: Celebrate only one religion in depth
Teach about multiple festivals, invite community members to explain meanings and focus on shared values like community and charity
questions.ex: Presenting multiple festivals and emphasizing shared social values maintains neutrality while teaching social cohesion.

questions.q: A policymaker asks you to prioritize interventions to reduce dropout in grades 6-8. Which combination is evidence-based?
options: Increase exam difficulty and reduce funding
Provide targeted scholarships, flexible school schedules, adolescent-friendly sanitation and life skills programs
Focus solely on tertiary scholarship programs
questions.ex: Scholarships, flexible timing, improved sanitation and life skills address common dropout causes among adolescents.

questions.q: How should a teacher evaluate whether their lesson fostered higher-order thinking in grade 5?
options: Only check whether students can recite facts
Analyze student work for evidence of reasoning, problem-solving steps and ability to justify answers
questions.ex: Examining student artifacts for reasoning and justification provides concrete evidence of higher-order thinking outcomes.

questions.q: In a multilingual classroom, standardized tests in one language disadvantage some students. As an assessment designer, what alternative maintains comparability while reducing bias?
options: Allow language accommodations (bilingual glossaries), use performance-based tasks and include language-appropriate norming
Use only the dominant language always
questions.ex: Accommodations, performance tasks and appropriate norming reduce bias while enabling valid comparisons across groups.

questions.q: A curriculum developer must integrate 21st-century skills into grade 3 without overloading teachers. Which strategy is feasible?
options: Add an extra subject for 21st-century skills
Integrate skills through existing subjects with teacher guides, sample activities and simple assessment rubrics
Require extensive separate training with no classroom support
questions.ex: Embedding skills into existing subjects with practical guides and rubrics supports teachers without adding workload.

questions.q: You are evaluating textbooks for cultural inclusivity. Which evaluation criterion is most important?
options: Representation of diverse roles, accurate local contexts and non-stereotypical portrayals
questions.ex: Key criteria include diverse, accurate and non-stereotypical representation to ensure cultural inclusivity.

questions.q: A teacher must respond to students sharing traumatic events related to floods. Which immediate classroom action is appropriate?
options: Probe for details in front of class
Provide a safe space, listen empathetically, offer appropriate support and refer to counseling services
Punish students for bringing it up
questions.ex: Empathetic listening, creating safety and referral to support services are appropriate responses to trauma disclosures.

questions.q: Which sociological measure helps a district identify schools that need resource reallocation to promote equity?
options: Only average test scores across the province
Disaggregated data by socioeconomic status, gender, location and disability to reveal gaps
questions.ex: Disaggregated indicators reveal inequities and guide targeted resource allocation to underserved groups.

questions.q: A teacher uses narrative storytelling to teach moral reasoning. How can assessment capture students' moral development progress?
options: Use scenario-based prompts asking students to propose actions, justify choices and reflect on consequences over time
questions.ex: Scenario-based prompts that require justification and reflection measure moral reasoning rather than surface storytelling skills.

questions.q: In reforming assessment policy, how can external examinations be aligned with classroom-based assessment to support learning?
options: Standardize competencies, provide exemplars, align curricula and encourage school-based continuous assessment feeding into external results
Rely only on high-stakes single tests
questions.ex: Alignment requires shared competencies, exemplars and integration of classroom assessments to inform and prepare students for external exams.

subcategories.title: Child Development and Educational Psychology - easy
subcategories.subject: Child Development and Educational Psychology

questions.q: Which developmental domain focuses on children's ability to recognize and manage emotions and form relationships?
questions.ex: Emotional and social development involves understanding emotions, managing behavior, and building relationships.

questions.q: Piaget is best known for which theory?
questions.ex: Jean Piaget proposed stages of cognitive development describing how children's thinking changes with age.

questions.q: Which stage in Piaget’s theory typically includes children aged 2 to 7 years?
questions.ex: The preoperational stage (2–7 years) features symbolic play and egocentrism but limited logical reasoning.

questions.q: Which psychologist is associated with behaviorism and classical conditioning?
questions.ex: Ivan Pavlov discovered classical conditioning through experiments with dogs and conditioned reflexes.

questions.q: What does 'scaffolding' refer to in education?
options: Temporary support to help learner progress
questions.ex: Scaffolding provides temporary support from teachers or peers to help learners achieve tasks beyond current ability.

questions.q: At what age do children typically begin to walk independently?
questions.ex: Most children begin independent walking around 9–15 months, commonly within 6–12 months range.

questions.q: Which area assesses how a child uses words and sentences?
questions.ex: Language development covers vocabulary, sentence structure, and communication skills.

questions.q: What is 'reinforcement' in behaviorist theory?
options: A cognitive strategy for solving problems
questions.ex: Reinforcement refers to consequences that increase the likelihood a behavior will be repeated.

questions.q: Which concept refers to differences in how children learn and behave?
questions.ex: Individual differences capture variability among children in abilities, temperament, and learning styles.

questions.q: Which stage in Erikson’s theory applies to school-age children learning competence?
questions.ex: Industry vs. Inferiority (school-age) focuses on mastering skills and developing competence.

questions.q: What is an example of a fine motor skill?
questions.ex: Cutting with scissors requires fine motor control of hands and fingers.

questions.q: Which term describes a child's natural tendency to become attached to caregivers?
questions.ex: Attachment is the emotional bond that develops between a child and caregiver.

questions.q: Who emphasized the importance of social interaction for cognitive development (zone of proximal development)?
questions.ex: Vygotsky highlighted social interaction and the zone of proximal development as central to learning.

questions.q: What is an appropriate classroom strategy for young children with short attention spans?
questions.ex: Short activities and movement help maintain engagement for young children.

questions.q: Which term describes learning by watching and imitating others?
questions.ex: Observational learning (Bandura) involves learning through modeling others' behavior.

questions.q: Which measure typically estimates a child’s general intellectual ability?
questions.ex: IQ tests aim to estimate cognitive abilities relative to age norms.

questions.q: What is 'critical period' in development?
options: A time when learning is impossible
A window when certain abilities are easily acquired
A phase of punishment for mistakes
questions.ex: A critical period is a timeframe when specific skills (e.g., language) are more readily acquired.

questions.q: Which classroom practice supports language development in early grades?
questions.ex: Oral language, storytelling, and discussion foster vocabulary and communication skills.

questions.q: What does 'metacognition' mean?
questions.ex: Metacognition involves awareness and regulation of one's cognitive processes.

questions.q: Which condition is characterized by difficulty sustaining attention and hyperactivity?
questions.ex: ADHD includes symptoms of inattention and/or hyperactivity-impulsivity.

questions.q: Which approach emphasizes student choice, self-actualization, and personal growth?
questions.ex: Humanistic approaches focus on individual growth, choice, and self-actualization.

questions.q: What is an appropriate response when a child shows frustration with a task?
options: Provide encouragement and break task into steps
questions.ex: Encouragement and task segmentation reduce frustration and support success.

questions.q: Which factor is most likely to affect early brain development?
questions.ex: Nutrition and caregiving strongly influence early brain growth and development.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of positive reinforcement in class?
options: Sending a student out of class
questions.ex: Praise following desired behavior increases the likelihood the behavior will recur.

questions.q: Which intelligence theory proposes multiple distinct intelligences like linguistic and kinesthetic?
questions.ex: Howard Gardner proposed multiple intelligences, including linguistic and bodily-kinesthetic.
